<div>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name="ExplanatoryNote_012455"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">EXPLANATORY NOTE</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We previously restated our annual and quarterly
consolidated financial statements as reflected in our annual report on
Form&nbsp;10-K for the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;3, 2005, and our
quarterly reports on Form&nbsp;10-Q for the quarterly periods ended April&nbsp;4,
2005, July&nbsp;4, 2005 and October&nbsp;3, 2005 (collectively, the &#147;Reports&#146;&#146;)
and in connection therewith disclosed in our Form&nbsp;8-K filed on
April&nbsp;26, 2005, our intention to amend our quarterly reports on Form&nbsp;10-Q
for the quarterly periods ended March&nbsp;29, 2004, June&nbsp;28, 2004 and
September&nbsp;27, 2004 (collectively, the &#147;2004 Form&nbsp;10-Qs&#146;&#146;) to include
the restated financial statements for the relevant periods. Upon further
analysis and consideration of the information contained in the Reports and prevailing
disclosure practices, we have determined that full disclosure of the
restatements has been provided and therefore amendments to the 2004
Form&nbsp;10-Qs are not necessary under the circumstances. In this regard, we
note that our quarterly reports on Form&nbsp;10-Q for the quarterly periods
ended April&nbsp;4, 2005, July&nbsp;4, 2005 and October&nbsp;3, 2005 contained
restated financial information for the quarterly periods ended March&nbsp;29,
2004, June&nbsp;28, 2004 and September&nbsp;27, 2004, respectively. We also
note that the consolidated financial statements as of and for the fiscal&#160; year ended January&nbsp;3, 2005 contained in
our annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;3, 2005
were not restated. Accordingly, as disclosed in our Form&nbsp;8-K filed on
April&nbsp;26, 2005, the consolidated financial statements contained in the
2004 Form 10-Qs should not be relied upon.</font></p>

 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">4</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='4',FILE='C:\fc\9313271640_D12364_993395\7678-1-ca.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Apr  3 13:27 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item1_Business__074002"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 1.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Business.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="General_074002"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">General</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Restaurant Group,&nbsp;Inc.
was incorporated in Delaware in October&nbsp;1997. Prior to October&nbsp;1997,
our operations were conducted through The New York Restaurant Group, LLC (&#147;NYRG&#148;),
our predecessor limited liability company. During October&nbsp;1997, NYRG
merged with SWRG.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are a developer, owner and operator of middle to high-end,
high-volume restaurants in the United States. Our core concept is Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky, a classic American restaurant. Management believes Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky is a recognized brand name in the upscale segment of the restaurant
industry. At January&nbsp;2, 2006, we operated 14 restaurants, eleven of which
were owned and three of which were managed. We own nine of the ten Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurants we operate. In addition we own a Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky unit in New Orleans, Louisiana (&#147;S&amp;W of New Orleans&#148;), which
closed on&#160; August&nbsp;29, 2005 due to
Hurricane Katrina. At this time, we are unable to determine when this
restaurant will reopen and are currently evaluating our options. We also own
our new concept, Quality Meats, a contemporary American restaurant that is
located in the space previously occupied by the Manhattan Ocean Club. We closed
the Manhattan Ocean Club on January&nbsp;1, 2006 and expect to open Quality
Meats in the second quarter of 2006. We believe that each of our restaurants
offers distinctive high quality food, creative menus, an extensive wine
selection and exceptional customer service accompanied by attractive design and
decor. We believe that the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky and Wollensky&#146;s Grill restaurant
concepts have broad national appeal and that, as a result, we have considerable
opportunities to expand our business. We believe that we currently operate in
one business segment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 1977, the original Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
restaurant, which we manage, opened in New York City. Three years later, we
developed The Post House, a distinctive steak and chop house with an American
theme that we currently manage. In 1989, we opened Cit&#233;, a Parisian grand-caf&#233;
style restaurant. The Park Avenue Caf&#233; concept, begun in 1992, combines seasonal
new American cuisine in a caf&#233; atmosphere, while Maloney&nbsp;&amp; Porcelli,
which we developed in 1996 and currently manage, presents updated classic
American cuisine. Our owned and managed restaurants have received local and
national dining awards, including the Distinguished Restaurants of North
America &#147;DiRoNA Award&#148; and Wine Spectator&#146;s &#147;Grand Award.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006, the average
sales for our nine owned Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants open for the
entire period were $10.0&nbsp;million per restaurant. Sales for the year ended January&nbsp;2,
2006 for the managed Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant in New York were
$26.5&nbsp;million, for which we received $609,000 as a management fee. For the
year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006, average sales for all of our thirteen consolidated
restaurants open for the full period (which includes the sales for Maloney&nbsp;&amp;
Porcelli, a restaurant we manage) were $9.4&nbsp;million per restaurant.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="OperatingStrategy_074002"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating Strategy</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that the key to our future success is our
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky and Wollensky&#146;s Grill restaurant concepts that are
focused on the middle to high-end segment of the restaurant industry. To
achieve our goal, we are pursuing the following operating strategies:</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursue Disciplined Restaurant Growth in 2007 and
Beyond</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although we do not have any leases signed other than
leases relating to our existing locations, we plan to resume our growth in 2007
with the launch of our first free-standing Wollensky&#146;s Grill (individually, a &#147;Grill&#148;
and collectively, &#147;Grills&#148;). We plan to open a total of three to four Grills
from 2007 to 2008. The menus and atmosphere of the Grills will be updated from
the original Wollensky&#146;s Grill, which opened in 1980, adjacent to the flagship
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky location in New York City. Although the growth focus
will be on opening Grills, we will continue to look at opportunities to open
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky units.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">5</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='5',FILE='C:\fc\9313271640_D12364_993395\7678-1-ca.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Apr  3 13:27 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our cash investment for each of our owned Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurants open as of January&nbsp;2, 2006, net of landlord
contributions, averaged approximately $6.8&nbsp;million, excluding pre-opening
costs, and our Smith and Wollensky restaurants averaged approximately 19,000
square feet. When we resume our growth in 2007, we expect that each Grill
restaurant will range between 7,000 and 9,000 square feet and will require a cash
investment of approximately $2.5 million, net of landlord contributions and
excluding pre-opening expenses. The estimate of the amount of our cash
investment assumes that the property on which each new unit is located is being
leased and is dependent on the size of the location and the amount of the
landlord contribution.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Focus on Prominent Locations</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that the locations of our restaurants are
critical to our long-term success, and we devote significant time and resources
to analyzing each prospective site. In general, we prefer to open our Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurants on sites near central business districts within larger
metropolitan areas. For our Grill concept, we plan on evaluating sites not only
within larger metropolitan areas, but also within midsize communities. In
addition to carefully analyzing demographic information for each prospective
site, management considers factors such as visibility, traffic patterns,
accessibility, adequacy of parking facilities, tourist volume, volume of business
travelers, convention business, local competition, and proximity to shopping
areas, office towers, parks and hotels.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Improve Operating Cash Flows</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We will focus on increasing our cash position by
improving our operating cash flows, while limiting our maintenance capital
expenditures on existing Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants. We intend to
further increase our operating cash flows from our mature and recently opened
restaurants by adding per unit sales volume while maintaining effective cost
controls in our mature restaurants and by getting the most recently opened
restaurants to operate at cost levels consistent with our mature restaurants.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Commitment to Superior Quality Food and Wine</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that a primary element of our appeal to our
customers is our reputation for quality menus, creative presentations of
carefully prepared food and extensive wine selections. We employ a chef at each
of our restaurants who ensures the high quality of the food served. Our
restaurants feature USDA prime grade beef, dry-aged and butchered on the
premises, top-quality seafood and high quality ingredients purchased daily in
local marketplaces. Each of our restaurants bakes some of their own bread on
the premises and features highly trained pastry chefs who prepare a range of
traditional desserts and specialty confections.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our commitment to fine wines is evident in our
extensive inventory. Our owned and managed restaurants have an aggregate of
over 110,000 bottles of wine and average more than 500 wine listings per
restaurant. Each restaurant has its own beverage and/or wine manager who is
supported at the corporate management level by our wine department.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Capitalize on Brand Awareness and Customer Loyalty</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that our significant investment in
marketing and advertising programs has contributed to what management believes
is a national awareness of our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants. Our
marketing strategy is designed to build a loyal customer base, to enhance a
strong identity and name recognition for our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
restaurants, to generate positive word-of-mouth advertising and to create
opportunities to cross-promote our restaurants. We have implemented this
strategy through the use of advertising, promotional activity and cross-marketing
of our restaurants. We run full-page&nbsp;advertisements in leading national
publications, including The New York Times. We also employ an advertising
strategy that focuses on national golf including a commercial currently
featuring golf pro Craig Stadler. In addition, we hold creative promotional
events such as &#147;Wine Week&#153;&#148;, a popular semi-annual event, restaurant </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">6</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">opening galas and
concierge dinners. We have enhanced our name recognition and brand awareness
through our comprehensive merchandising strategy, which includes the sale of
our sauces, salad dressings, knives and cookbooks. Our sauces, which include
steak, barbecue and pepper, are now offered at over 4,000 wholesale and retail
stores.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Provide Exceptional Customer Service</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are committed to
providing our customers attentive and professional service through employees
trained to exceed guests&#146; expectations. We believe that our brand recognition,
high unit sales volume and high average checks enable us to attract talented
managers, chefs and wait staff. Each restaurant is staffed with an experienced
team of managers, kitchen personnel and wait staff, many of whom have a long
tenure with us. Most of our general managers have at least 20&nbsp;years of
work experience in the restaurant industry. Restaurant personnel are instructed
in various areas of restaurant management, including food quality and
preparation, wine selection, customer service and beverage service. In
addition, our ability to offer opportunities for promotion and training by
experienced managers enhances our recruiting and training efforts. We believe
our low rate of employee turnover contributes to consistent quality and
attentive customer service.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Provide Experienced Management Support</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our senior executive team
is comprised of Alan Stillman, our founder and Chief Executive Officer, Samuel
Goldfinger, our Chief Financial Officer and Eugene Zuriff, our President. Alan
Stillman has been with us for over 25&nbsp;years, has opened numerous
restaurants and is highly experienced in the creation and implementation of
restaurant concepts and has been creating restaurant concepts, including T.G.I.
Friday&#146;s and other restaurant concepts, for over 30&nbsp;years. Our restaurant
general managers, most of whom are drawn from our restaurant personnel, have an
average tenure with us of over 17&nbsp;years, and most of them have worked in
the restaurant industry for at least 20&nbsp;years. In addition to our general
managers, we currently employ approximately 220 restaurant management personnel
and we believe they will be a substantial source of managerial talent as we
expand.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="TheSmithWollenskyAndWollenskysGri_102531"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky and Wollensky&#146;s Grill Concepts</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky concept, a dining
experience that provides high quality selections in an upscale environment, was
started in 1977 with the opening of the first Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant
in New York City. The Wollensky&#146;s Grill concept will be updated from the
original Wollensky&#146;s Grill, which opened in 1980, adjacent to the flagship
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky location New York City. The Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurant in New York typifies our approach to the concept and has
been described by Gourmet magazine as the &#147;quintessential New York steakhouse.&#148;
The essential elements of the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky and Wollensky&#146;s Grill
concepts are:</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Critically Acclaimed Food</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We strive to provide our customers with the best
quality cuisine. Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants feature USDA prime
grade beef served in generous portions. Unlike most other high-end restaurants,
each Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant dry ages and butchers substantially
all its beef on the premises. During this dry aging process, which takes three
to four weeks to complete, the beef generally loses approximately 10% to 20% of
its weight. Although the dry aging process is expensive and time consuming, we
believe it produces a more flavorful and tender steak than alternative
processes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our menu also offers the highest quality seafood,
including three- to thirteen-pound lobsters, fish, veal, lamb, pork
and poultry. Freshly baked bread is served as well. Complementing our
substantial main courses, our dessert menu features traditional desserts such
as cheesecake and chocolate<b><font style="font-weight:bold;"> </font></b>cake, as well
as other specialized confections prepared on location by our highly trained
pastry chefs.</font></p>

<div>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Extensive Wine Selection</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fine wine is an integral part of the Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky dining experience. Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants boast an
extensive wine inventory of over 85,000 bottles, and our Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky in New York, which has over 15,000 bottles of wine, received Wine
Spectator&#146;s &#147;Grand Award&#148; each year from 1987 through 1994, Wine Spectator&#146;s &#147;Award
of Excellence&#148; from 1995 through 2005, and received Wine Enthusiast &#147;Award of
Ultimate Distinction&#148; in 2006. The Great American Wine list features on average
over 600 selections with a combination of the country&#146;s most renowned wineries,
alongside a selection of undiscovered gems, which are lesser known names of
outstanding quality. Our nationally acclaimed wine programs, such as &#147;Wine
Week&#153;,&#148; have been written about extensively by The New York Times and Wine
Spectator.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Distinctive Design and Decor</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that a unique decor is essential to the
creation of a fine dining experience for the customer. Each of our Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurants has a decor that features hardwood floors, polished brass
and dark wood accents and authentic folk-art from 1900-1940 Americana.
Menus are presented under glass in stained wooden frames, while blackboards
located around the dining rooms display signature menu items and daily
specials. Each restaurant&#146;s exterior, complete with traditional awnings,
incorporates Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky&#146;s signature green and white colors. In
addition to the distinctive decor, our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants
feature a design layout that creates small dining areas and enhances
efficiency. Our large square footage is broken into small areas that create a
more private dining experience while maintaining a large seating capacity. In
order to ensure the hottest food and most efficient service, each Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurant has kitchens located on each floor except for one of the
four levels at our Boston location. This flexible design allows us to close off
sections of our restaurants, and thus reduce operating costs, during non-peak
hours or days.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also offer customers a chance to view our chefs in
action. Each Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky, other than the Philadelphia location,
has either a &#147;kitchen table&#148; in a glass-enclosed area inside of the main
kitchen or a table located just outside the kitchen with a view into the
kitchen. Customers at these tables can eat, drink wine and watch our expert
chefs prepare dinner. Additionally, most of our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
locations offer some outdoor dining.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wollensky&#146;s Grill</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain of our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky&#146;s incorporate
a Wollensky&#146;s Grill, a more informal alternative which offers menu selections
similar to those offered at Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky in smaller, lower-priced
portions, as well as hamburgers and sandwiches. Wollensky&#146;s Grill provides
flexibility for Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky, and the two dining areas have the
ability to expand and contract relative to one another to accommodate customer
demand. Wollensky&#146;s Grill generally has a separate entrance and offers expanded
late-night hours. A Wollensky&#146;s Grill typically seats up to 125 customers. In
some of our locations, Wollensky&#146;s Grill and its menu are combined with the
main dining space with no separate Wollensky&#146;s Grill area.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We plan to resume our growth in 2007 with the launch
of our first free-standing Wollensky&#146;s Grill. We plan to open a total of three
to four Grills from 2007 to 2008. The menus and atmosphere of the Grills will
be updated from the original Wollensky&#146;s Grill, which opened in 1980, adjacent
to the flagship Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky in New York City. Although our
growth focus will be on opening Grills, we will continue to look at
opportunities to open Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky units.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Private Dining Facilities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All of our owned Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
restaurants have dedicated private dining facilities. These facilities host numerous
events that generate higher per-person average checks than our restaurants. In </font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>This location is managed
not owned.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>This
location was closed on&#160; August&nbsp;29,
2005 due to the damages caused by Hurricane Katrina. At this time, we are
unable to determine when this &#160;restaurant
will reopen and are currently evaluating our options.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="GrowthStrategy_074230"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Growth Strategy</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our current objective is to increase sales from our
existing restaurant operations as we build upon and increase what we believe is
our reputation for providing an exceptional dining experience and high-quality
food. At the same time, we plan to leverage our experience in developing and
operating restaurants by introducing our Wollensky&#146;s Grill restaurant concept
into new markets in 2007 and beyond.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Grow and Develop Existing Restaurants</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since December&nbsp;1997, we have opened ten Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurants. Our experience has shown that our restaurants take
between 15 and 36&nbsp;months to achieve expected company-wide targeted levels
of performance. Some of our newer restaurants are currently in various stages
of the ramp-up phase, and we believe incremental sales and restaurant level operating
profitability can be realized from each of these restaurants as they continue
to develop.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Leverage Centralized Operations to Increase
Profitability</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have established a central corporate infrastructure
to manage our restaurants through which we seek to take advantage of volume
discounts and the allocation of fixed costs over a larger revenue base. All of
our restaurants report daily through a point-of-sale system that allows us to
monitor our sales, costs, inventory and other operating statistics. As we
continue our expansion, we will seek to take advantage of even greater volume
discounts.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Expand Retail Offerings and Develop Branded
Merchandise</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have developed a comprehensive merchandising
strategy to reinforce and capitalize on what we believe is a distinctive
upscale brand image built on the quality and name recognition of our Smith&nbsp;&amp;
</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">9</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='9',FILE='C:\fc\8921332520_D12364_981337\7678-1-cc.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 30 21:03 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Wollensky restaurants. At
our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants and on our website, selected
products are offered for sale under the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky brand name,
including custom steak knives, steak, barbeque and pepper sauce, salad
dressings and cookbooks. Sales of items incorporating the Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky name are subject to the payment of a royalty to St. James Associates,
the partnership that owns the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant in New York</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursue Disciplined Restaurant Growth in New Markets in
2007 and Beyond</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although we currently do not have any leases signed
other than leases relating to our existing locations, we plan to resume our
growth in 2007 with the launch of our first free-standing Grill. We plan to
open a total of three to four Grills from 2007 to 2008. The menus and
atmosphere of the Grills will be updated from the original Wollensky&#146;s Grill,
which opened in 1980, adjacent to the flagship Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
location in New York City. Although the growth focus will be on opening Grills,
we will continue to look at opportunities to open Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
units. We expect that each Grill restaurant will range between 7,000 and 9,000
square feet and will require a cash investment of approximately $2.5&nbsp;million,
net of landlord contributions and excluding pre-opening expenses. The estimate
of the amount of our cash investment assumes that the property on which each
new unit is located is being leased and is dependent on the size of the
location and the amount of the landlord contribution.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In general, we prefer to open our Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurants on sites near central business districts within larger
metropolitan areas. For our Grill concept, we plan on evaluating sites not only
within lager metropolitan areas, but also within midsize communities. Typically,
prior to opening a new restaurant our management team carefully analyzes
demographic information for each prospective site and considers other factors.
After reviewing all of the relevant information, management will rate a city&#146;s
appropriateness as a location for a Wollensky&#146;s Grill.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We seek long-term leases providing for substantial
development or rent contributions from landlords or real estate developers in
exchange for a market based minimum annual rent and/or a percentage of annual
gross sales above a stipulated minimum. We also evaluate opportunities to
purchase or lease, and renovate existing restaurant sites that satisfy our
selection criteria. Use of such sites can significantly reduce construction
costs, shorten the time required to open a new restaurant and increase the
return on investment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have developed a
restaurant opening program and team designed to optimize the performance of our
new restaurants. The team includes a general manager, training manager,
purchasing manager, beverage manager and chef/kitchen manager. Restaurant
managers typically complete a one to three month training program and we rotate
certain of the senior managers of our established restaurants to a new
restaurant during the course of the first three months it is in operation in
order to ensure quality control.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="UnitEconomics_102619"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unit Economics</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">While we seek to develop
high profile locations that create a distinctive dining experience, we are able
to maintain unit operating margins due to high sales volumes coupled with
effective cost controls. For the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006, the average
sales for our nine owned Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants open for the
full period were $10.0&nbsp;million. Sales for the year ended January&nbsp;2,
2006 for the managed Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant in New York were
$26.5&nbsp;million, for which we received $609,000 as a management fee. For the
year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006, average sales for all of our thirteen
consolidated restaurants open for the full period were $9.4&nbsp;million per
restaurant. Our average cash investment, net of landlord contributions, was
approximately $6.8 million for the ten owned Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
restaurants open as of January&nbsp;2, 2006, excluding pre-opening costs. We
expect that each free-standing Grill restaurant, which will range between 7,000
and 9,000 square feet, will require a cash investment of approximately $2.5
million, net of landlord contributions and excluding pre-opening expenses. The
estimate of the amount of our cash </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">investment
assumes that the property on which each new unit is located is being leased and

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="OurOtherRestaurantConcepts_102633"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Other Restaurant Concepts</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>This location is managed
not owned.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>This location is owned.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>This location was closed
on January&nbsp;1, 2006 and is expected to re-open under the name &#147;Quality
Meats&#148; during April&nbsp;2006 with a seating capacity of approximately 190.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>This location is located
in Chicago, Illinois. We currently only receive a fee for the right of its
owner to use the name &#147;Mrs.&nbsp;Parks Tavern&#148;.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(5)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>This
location is managed not owned, but the accounts and results of the entity that
owns this location are consolidated pursuant to the adoption of FASB
Interpretation No.&nbsp;46 (revised December&nbsp;2003), &#147;Consolidation of
Variable Interest Entities&#148; (&#147;FIN 46 (R)&#148;). See Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements, Note 2.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="MarketingAdvertisingAndPromotions_074232"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Marketing,
Advertising and Promotions</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the past 20&nbsp;years, the goal of our marketing
strategy has been to build a loyal customer base, to enhance what we believe is
the strong identity and name recognition of our restaurants, to generate
positive word-of-mouth advertising and to create opportunities to cross-promote
our restaurants. In order to attract new customers, we focus primarily on
television advertising including a commercial currently featuring golf pro
Craig Stadler. We also employ limited radio and print advertising. We achieve
national as well as local exposure through our print campaign.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that our commitment to advertising sets us
apart from other upscale restaurants, and that our advertising expenditures are
substantially greater than that of comparable high-end restaurants. We also
take advantage of opportunities to cross-promote our restaurants by
publishing advertisements and marketing materials featuring all of our
restaurants as a group.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Not only do we advertise directly to the general
public, but we also offer specific customer services that have the potential
for repeated referrals. Our restaurants host parties for the concierges of
nearby hotels that are designed to enhance each restaurant&#146;s name recognition
and reputation for quality and service, thereby encouraging concierge recommendations.
Additionally, our wait staff selectively provides complimentary food and drinks
to customers, further developing customer loyalty.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">11</font></p>
</div><br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='11',FILE='C:\fc\8921332520_D12364_981337\7678-1-cc.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 30 21:03 2006' -->



<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">

<div>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are continually strengthening our name recognition
and brand identity, particularly in new markets. In conjunction with restaurant
openings, we host dinners, lunches and cocktail parties for various civic,
philanthropic and charitable organizations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also host Wine Week&#153;,
which we started in 1986. Wine Week&#153; has evolved into &#147;National Wine Weeks&#153;&#148;
which we hold twice a year, usually in March&nbsp;and September. Our
restaurants sponsor wine tastings at lunch each day for the entire week and
wine makers are invited to represent their wineries and to serve and discuss
their wines with customers. We believe these events enhance our restaurants&#146;
reputations for dedication to maintaining superior quality wine lists. Our
other promotions include various tasting events as well as dinners hosted by
nationally renowned chefs. We believe that our promotions build customer
loyalty and increase future sales at our restaurants.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="RestaurantOperationsAndManagement_112140"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restaurant
Operations and Management</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that our high unit sales volume and
portfolio of concepts allow us to attract, compensate and maintain
high-quality, experienced restaurant management and personnel. We believe that
we have a low rate of staff turnover for the restaurant industry. Professional,
efficient and attentive service is integral to our overall success. Each of our
restaurants is operated as an independent facility with each restaurant&#146;s
general manager exercising discretion and playing a key role in its success.
The general managers in our restaurants have an average tenure with us of over
17&nbsp;years. During training, restaurant personnel are instructed in various
areas of restaurant management, including food quality and preparation, wine
selection, customer service, beverage service, quality and cost controls and
employee relations. Restaurant general managers are also provided with
operations manuals relating to food and beverage preparation and operation of
restaurants. These manuals are designed to ensure that we will provide uniform
operations in each of our restaurants, high-quality products on a consistent
basis and proper service.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have developed a restaurant opening program and
team designed to optimize the performance of our new restaurants. The team
includes a general manager, training manager, purchasing manager, beverage
manager and chef/kitchen manager. All of these employees currently fill
functions within our organization, but will be available to open new
restaurants when we do resume our growth. Restaurant managers typically
complete a one to three month training program and we rotate certain of the
senior managers of our established restaurants to a new restaurant during the
course of the first three months it is in operation in order to ensure quality
control. Management believes it is imperative for new managers to spend much of
their training period side by side with managers in existing operations in
order to gain critical insight into day-to-day operations and overall
management philosophy. The director of operations and the local restaurant
manager interview all staff on site. Chefs are brought to an established unit
for training prior to an opening, and periodically are given the opportunity to
work at other locations under the supervision of our critically acclaimed
chefs. The director of management information systems typically stays at each
new location until all accounting and management information systems are fully
operational. We also coordinate our marketing, advertising and promotional
program to support new restaurant openings while at the same time building
national brand recognition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">New wait staff at our
restaurants participate in training during which time they work under the close
supervision of our corporate opening team. Wait staff are trained and tested on
proper service technique, wine and food knowledge, customer satisfaction and
point-of-sale system usage.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Purchasing_112144"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchasing</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability to maintain consistent quality throughout
our restaurants depends in part upon our ability to acquire food products and
related items from reliable sources in accordance with our specifications. To
ensure continuity of pricing and quality throughout all of our restaurants, we
maintain on-premise stewards at most of our restaurants who are supported by a
corporate purchasing department.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">12</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='12',FILE='C:\fc\8862130370_D11241_971586\7678-1-ce.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 29 06:21 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We attempt to maintain a consistent food and beverage
cost as a percentage of sales through a variety of means. We have gained a
great knowledge of trends and fluctuations in the pricing of our key
commodities based on over 25&nbsp;years of experience. While we do not believe
most market conditions warrant entering long-term pricing contracts on our
primary items, we contract or lock into appropriate volume commitments. We lock
pricing and volume availability on key items such as beef and shrimp, which
represent a majority of our food cost, when we deem it beneficial. We have on
occasion attempted modest hedges against volatility in the price of beef. Under
extreme circumstances, such as the aftermath of the single case of mad cow
disease reported in December&nbsp;2003, we may experience significant cost
volatility. Although we do not have a single source of supply for any
particular food item and we believe that adequate alternative sources of supply
are readily available, these alternative sources might not provide as favorable
terms to us as our current suppliers when viewed on a long-term basis. In
addition, we believe we are able to achieve cost savings through purchasing
restaurant items such as glass, china, silver, utensils and similar items and
equipment and some food items for all restaurants through Company wide
agreements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each of our restaurants also has an in-store beverage
manager and/or wine manager who is supported by our corporate wine department.
The beverage manager or wine manager at each restaurant purchases the majority
of the wine in the local markets for each restaurant. Although the beverage
manager may tailor some of the wine selections to customer preferences, market
availability and menu/wine pairing, our Great-American Wine List forms the core
of our selections at the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky locations. We have several
national programs with wineries creating pricing programs to support local
purchasing.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We devote considerable
attention to controlling food costs. We make use of information technology and
each of our restaurants&#146; point-of-sale system, providing us with precise
information on daily sales and inventory needs, thus reducing our need to carry
large quantities of food inventory. This cost management system is complemented
by our ability to obtain volume-based discounts. Additionally, as we open
additional restaurants, we expect to be able to take further advantage of
volume discounts and other cost savings.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ManagementArrangements_112148"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management Arrangements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to our management arrangements, we provide
new restaurant concept design, construction, staff training, menu development,
administration, managerial and operating services to the restaurants we manage.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky.</font></i></font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i>We
manage the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant in New York pursuant to a
management agreement with St.&nbsp;James Associates. The agreement continues
until terminated by the parties in accordance with the terms of the agreement
described below. Pursuant to the management agreement, we provide management
services to the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant in New York in exchange
for a fee of 2.3% of all restaurant sales of the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
restaurant in New York. Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Operating Corp., an entity
controlled by Mr.&nbsp;Stillman, is one of the two general partners of
St.&nbsp;James Associates. Mr.&nbsp;Stillman is also a limited partner of
St.&nbsp;James Associates. The other general partner of St.&nbsp;James
Associates may terminate the agreement if we fail to manage and market the restaurant
in the same manner as has been done since the opening of the restaurant in
1977, and do not cure any failure to do so within 30&nbsp;days after notice
from the other general partner. In addition, the other general partner may
terminate the agreement if we fail to prepare and deliver financial statements
to St.&nbsp;James Associates each month, and do not cure any failure to do so
within three days after notice from the other general partner. Additionally,
under the terms of the agreement, the other partner of St.&nbsp;James
Associates may terminate the agreement and replace us with any person, firm or
corporation chosen by the other general partner, if we cease to be operated and

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We initiate and record our
financial information for each restaurant through centralized accounting and
management information systems. We collect sales and related information daily
from each restaurant and we provide restaurant managers with operating
statements for their respective locations. We connect point-of-sale systems in
individual restaurants via secured data network to a central data repository in
the corporate office and have upgraded such point-of-sale systems to facilitate

manage a central database of frequent customers and maintain our website, which
includes the ability to sell all Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky branded products

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Competition_102738"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Competition</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The restaurant industry is
intensely competitive in all our markets. We compete on the basis of the taste,
quality and price of food offered, customer service, ambience, location and
overall dining experience. The restaurant business is often affected by changes
in consumer tastes and discretionary spending patterns, national and regional
economic conditions, demographic trends, adverse weather conditions, consumer
confidence in the economy, traffic patterns, the cost and availability of raw
material and labor, purchasing power, governmental regulations and local
competitive factors. Although we believe we compete favorably with respect to
each of these factors, some of our direct and indirect competitors are
well-established national, regional or local chains and some have substantially
greater financial, marketing, and other resources than we do. We also compete
with many other restaurant and retail establishments for site locations and
restaurant level employees.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ServiceMarksTrademarksAndLicenseA_102739"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Service
Marks, Trademarks and License Agreements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have registered with the United States Patent and
Trademark Office the names &#147;Maloney and Porcelli&#148;&#160; &#147;Wine Week&#148; and &#147;National Wine Week.&#148;&#160; In addition, our subsidiary, La Cit&#233;
Associates, L.L.C., has registered the names &#147;Cit&#233;&#148; and &#147;Cit&#233; Grill,&#148; and
another of our subsidiaries, Atlantic&nbsp;&amp; Pacific Grill Associates, LLC,
has registered the names &#147;Park Avenue Caf&#233;,&#148; &#147;Park Avenue Caf&#233; Swordfish Chop,&#148;
&#147;Swordfish Chop,&#148; and &#147;Mrs.&nbsp;Park&#146;s Tavern.&#148; The Manhattan Ocean Club
Associates, LLC, which is one of our subsidiaries, has registered the name &#147;The
Manhattan Ocean Club&#148;, and &#147;Quality Meats.&#148; We have also registered trademarks
in several foreign countries. Parade 59 Restaurant LLC, which is a subsidiary
of ours, has registered the name &#147;ONEc.p.s.&#148; In addition, pursuant to our
management agreement regarding Maloney&nbsp;&amp; Porcelli discussed above, we
are the exclusive owner of the name &#147;Maloney&nbsp;&amp; Porcelli&#148; and may use

materially affect our business. We believe that our trademarks and service

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;1996, we acquired an exclusive license
for the use of the names &#147;Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky,&#148; &#147;Wollensky&#146;s Grill,&#148; and
all associated service marks, trademarks, trade names and trade dress from
St.&nbsp;James Associates for $2.5 million (the &#147;Original Licensing Agreement&#148;).

limitations discussed below. We are aware of a restaurant located in South
Africa, which is named &#147;Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky.&#148; We are not associated with
this restaurant, and have not authorized the use of the name &#147;Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky&#148; to this restaurant under our license.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Original Licensing Agreement, St.&nbsp;James
Associates had reserved the exclusive right to use the licensed names, subject
to receiving our consent in specific circumstances, within a 100-mile
radius of the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky in New York, subject to our exclusive
right to use the name within a 10-mile radius of City Hall in
Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Consequently, we may not open new Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurants or pursue retailing or merchandising opportunities within
such reserved territory. We have the right to sublicense all or any portion of
our rights under the license agreement without the consent of St.&nbsp;James
Associates to an affiliate or any other entity so long as we exercise and
maintain managerial control over all restaurants owned by such entity in the
manner that we currently exercise managerial control over the New York Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurant. Each sublicense agreement that we execute must contain
specific provisions set forth in the licensing agreement and declare that the
sublicense will be deemed automatically assigned to St.&nbsp;James Associates
upon any lawful termination of the license agreement. In all other
circumstances, we must obtain the written consent of St.&nbsp;James Associates
to sublicense our rights under the license agreement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the Original Licensing Agreement, we are

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="GovernmentRegulation_102743"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Government Regulation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our business is subject to extensive federal, state
and local government regulations, including regulations relating to alcoholic
beverage control, the preparation and sale of food, public health and safety,
sanitation, building, zoning and fire codes. A significant percentage of the revenues
of each of the restaurants we own or manage are attributable to the sale of
alcoholic beverages. Each restaurant has appropriate licenses from regulatory
authorities allowing it to serve liquor and/or beer and wine, and each
restaurant has food service licenses from local health authorities. Our
licenses to serve alcoholic beverages must be renewed annually and each
restaurant is operated in accordance with standardized procedures designed to
assure compliance with all applicable codes and regulations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are subject, in some states, to &#147;dram shop&#148;
statutes which generally provide a person injured by an intoxicated person the
right to recover damages from an establishment which wrongfully served
alcoholic beverages to such person and we carry liquor liability coverage as
part of our existing comprehensive general liability insurance. The development
and construction of additional restaurants will be subject to compliance with
applicable zoning, land use and environmental regulations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are also subject to the
Fair Labor Standards Act, the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986 and
various state laws governing such matters as minimum wages, overtime, tip
credits and reporting and other working conditions. A significant number of our
hourly personnel are paid at rates related to the federal minimum wage. In
addition, the Federal Americans with Disabilities Act prohibits discrimination
on the basis of disability in public accommodations and employment.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Seasonality_102745"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Seasonality</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our business is seasonal
in nature depending on the region of the United States in which a particular
restaurant is located, with revenues generally being less in the third quarter
than in other quarters due to </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">reduced
summer volume and highest in the fourth quarter due to year-end and holiday
events. As we continue to expand in other locations, the seasonality pattern

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Employees_102746"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employees</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of January&nbsp;2, 2006

our restaurants, we had 1,735 employees, including 307 management personnel and
administrators at the restaurants. None of our employees are covered by
collective bargaining agreements. Management believes our relationships with
our employees are generally excellent.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="FinancialAndGeographicInformation_102748"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For information relating

Financial Data.&#148; All of our revenues are attributable to our operations in the
United States, and all of our long-lived assets are located in the United

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item1a_RiskFactors__112315"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 1A.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Risk
Factors.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following are the most
significant risk factors applicable to us:</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name="RisksRelatedToOurBusiness_102801"></a><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">RISKS
RELATED TO OUR BUSINESS</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Our unfamiliarity with new
markets may present risks, which could have a material adverse effect on our
future growth and profitability.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our strategy depends on our ability to successfully
expand our Wollensky&#146;s Grill brand into new markets in which we have no
operating experience. We began to open Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants
outside of New York City in 1997. Historically, new Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
restaurants opened in expanded markets generally take about 15 to 36 months to
achieve expected company-wide targeted levels of performance, and we expect our
new free-standing Grills to have a similar ramp-up period. This is due to
higher operating costs caused by temporary inefficiencies typically associated
with expanding into new regions and opening new restaurants, such as lack of
market awareness and acceptance and limited availability of experienced staff. As
a result, our continued expansion may result in an increase in our operating
costs. New markets may have different competitive conditions, consumer tastes
and discretionary spending patterns than our existing markets, which may cause
our restaurants in these new markets to be less successful than our restaurants
in our existing markets. We cannot assure you that restaurants in new markets
will be successful.</font></p>

<p style="margin:6.0pt 0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Our
success in profitably pursuing our strategy of expansion will depend on our
ability to open new restaurants efficiently. Our planned expansion involves a
number of risks, which could delay or prevent the opening of new restaurants.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our ability to open new restaurants efficiently is
subject to a number of factors beyond our control, including:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Selection
and availability of suitable restaurant sites;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Negotiation
of acceptable lease or purchase terms for such sites;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Negotiation
of reasonable construction contracts and adequate supervision of construction:</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Our
ability to secure required governmental permits and approvals for both
construction and operation;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Availability
of adequate capital;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>General
economic conditions.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Adverse
weather conditions.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We may not be successful in addressing these factors,
which could adversely affect our ability to open our planned new restaurants on
a timely basis, or at all. Delays in opening or failures to open planned new
restaurants could cause our business, results of operations and financial
condition to suffer.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Terrorism and war
may have material adverse effect on our business.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Terrorist attacks, such as the attacks that occurred
in New York and Washington, D.C. on September&nbsp;11, 2001, and other acts of
violence or war in the United States or abroad, such as the war in Iraq, may
affect the markets in which we operate and our business, results of operations
and financial conditions. The potential near-term and long-term effects these
events may have on our business operations, our customers, the markets in which
we operate and the economy is uncertain. Because the consequences of any terrorist
attacks, or any armed conflicts are unpredictable, we may not be able to
foresee events that could have an adverse effect on our markets or our
business.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our profitability
is dependent in large measure on food, beverage and supply costs which are not
within our control.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our profitability is dependent in large measure on our
ability to anticipate and react to changes in food, beverage and supply costs.
Various factors beyond our control, including climatic changes and government
regulations, may affect food and beverage costs. Specifically, our dependence
on frequent, timely deliveries of fresh beef, poultry, seafood and produce
subjects us to the risks of possible shortages or interruptions in supply
caused by adverse weather or other conditions, which could adversely affect the
availability and cost of any such items. We cannot assure you that we will be
able to anticipate or react to increasing food and supply costs in the future.
The failure to react to these increases could materially and adversely affect
our business, results of operations and financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The restaurant industry is affected by changes in
consumer preferences and discretionary spending patterns that could result in a
reduction in our revenues.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Consumer preferences could be affected by health
concerns about the consumption of beef, the primary item on our
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants&#146; menus, or by specific events such as
the outbreak of or scare caused by &#147;mad cow disease&#148;, the popularity of the
Atkins diet and the South Beach diet and changes in consumer preferences to a
&#147;carb consciousness&#148;. If we were to have to modify the emphasis on beef in our
restaurants&#146; menus, we may lose customers who would be less satisfied with a
modified menu, and we may not be able to attract a new customer base to
generate the necessary revenues to maintain our income from restaurant
operations. A change in our menus may also result in us having different
competitors. We may not be able to successfully compete against established
competitors in the general restaurant market. Our success also depends on
various factors affecting discretionary consumer spending, including economic
conditions, disposable consumer income, consumer confidence and the United
States participation in military activities. Adverse changes in these factors
could reduce our customer base and spending patterns, either of which could
reduce our revenues and results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We currently operate 14 restaurants, 11 of which we
own. Due to this relatively small number of restaurants, poor financial
performance at any owned restaurant could have a significant negative impact on
our profitability as a whole. In addition we own S&amp;W of New Orleans, which
was closed on August&nbsp;29, 2005 due to Hurricane Katrina. At this time, we
are unable to determine when this restaurant will reopen and are currently
evaluating our options. We also own our new concept, Quality Meats, a
contemporary American restaurant that is located in the space previously
occupied by the Manhattan Ocean Club. We closed the Manhattan Ocean Club on January&nbsp;1,
2006, and expect to open Quality Meats in the second quarter of 2006. Future
growth in sales and profits will depend to a substantial extent on our ability
to increase sales and profits at our restaurants open less than fifteen months,
to operate our existing restaurants at higher sales levels that generate equal
or higher operating profits and to increase the number of our restaurants. The
results achieved to date by our relatively small restaurant base may not be
indicative of the results of a larger number of restaurants in a more
geographically dispersed area with varied demographic characteristics. We
cannot assure you that we will be able to increase sales and profits at our
restaurants open less than 15 months, operate our existing restaurants at
higher sales levels that generate equal or higher operating profits or increase
the number of our restaurants sufficiently to offset the impact of poor
performance at any one restaurant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Our geographic concentration in
New York City could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of
operations and financial condition.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We currently operate five restaurants in New York
City, two of which we own. We also own our new concept, Quality Meats and
expect to open in the second quarter of 2006. As a result, we are particularly
susceptible to adverse trends and economic conditions in New York City,
including its labor market, which could have a negative impact on our
profitability as a whole. In addition, given our geographic concentration,
negative publicity regarding any of our restaurants in New York City could have
a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial
condition, as could other regional occurrences such as acts of terrorism, local
strikes, natural disasters or changes in laws or regulations.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Economic

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Acceptance
