million from our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky units in Dallas and Houston, Texas,
which opened in March&nbsp;2003,January&nbsp;2004, respectively, and to our
unit in Boston, Massachusetts, which opened in September&nbsp;2004. The
increase in consolidated restaurant sales was also due to a net increase in
comparable consolidated restaurant sales of $7.9&nbsp;million, or 8.0%. Since
2004 was a 53 week period and 2003 was a 52 week period, when comparing the
fiscal years on a weekly sales basis the increase in comparable consolidated
sales was 5.9%. Consolidated restaurant sales for the 53<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">rd</font>&#160;week of fiscal 2004 were approximately $2.1
million. The increase in comparable consolidated restaurant sales was primarily
due to an increase in sales of $6.5 million from our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
units open the entire year in 2004. The improvement is due to an increase in
the average check, related primarily to price increases, and, to a lesser
extent, an increase in business travel, tourism and banquet sales. The increase
in comparable consolidated restaurant sales was also due to a net increase of
$1.4 million at our consolidated restaurants in New York, which includes the
increase in sales of $1.3 million from the entity that owns <font size="2" style="font-size:9.5pt;">Maloney&nbsp;&amp; Porcelli</font>, which is
being consolidated pursuant to our adoption of FIN 46(R)&nbsp;for fiscal 2004
and included on an unaudited pro forma basis for fiscal 2003. The increase in
sales for the entity that owns <font size="2" style="font-size:9.5pt;">Maloney&nbsp;&amp;
Porcelli</font> was attributable to an increase in volume, average check
and, to a lesser extent, banquet sales.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Food
and Beverage Costs.</font></i></font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i>Food and
beverage costs increased $6.5&nbsp;million to $38.7&nbsp;million in 2004 from
$32.2&nbsp;million in 2003 (unaudited pro forma). Food and beverage costs as a
percentage of consolidated restaurant sales increased to 31.4% in 2004 from
31.1% in 2003. The increase in food and
beverage costs related primarily to approximately $4.1 million in food and
beverage costs for the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky units in Dallas, Texas, which
opened in March&nbsp;2003, Houston, Texas, which opened in January&nbsp;2004,
and our unit in Boston, Massachusetts, which opened in September&nbsp;2004. The
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky units in Houston and Boston experienced higher than
normal food and beverage costs as a percentage of sales as a result of initial
startup inefficiencies and a lower revenue base. As the Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky units in Houston and Boston mature, operating efficiencies are
expected to continue to improve and the food and beverage costs as a percentage
of sales for that unit are expected to decrease. The increase in cost is also related
to an increase in food cost at our comparable units of approximately $1.3&nbsp;million.
This increase related primarily to the increase in the cost of beef that we
incurred during the first nine months of 2004 as compared to 2003, and to a net
increase in customer volume at our comparable units.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Salaries
and Related Benefits.</font></i></font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i>Salaries
and related benefits increased $6.5&nbsp;million to $35.9&nbsp;million in 2004
from $29.5&nbsp;million in 2003 (unaudited pro forma). This increase was primarily due to our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky units
in Dallas, Texas, which opened in March&nbsp;2003, our unit in Houston, Texas,
which opened in January&nbsp;2004, and our unit in Boston Massachusetts, which
opened in September&nbsp;2004. The increase relating to these units was $4.2
million. Salaries and related benefits as a percent of consolidated restaurant
sales increased to 29.2% in 2004 from 28.5% in 2003. The increase in salaries
and related benefits as a percentage of consolidated restaurant sales was
primarily due to the additional staffing required at the Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky units in Houston, Texas and Boston, Massachusetts during the unit
openings. It is common for our restaurants to experience increased costs for
additional staffing in the first six months of operations. Generally, as the
unit matures, operating efficiency is expected to improve as we expect that
staffing will be reduced through efficiencies and salaries and wages as a
percentage of consolidated sales for that unit will decrease due to the lower
staffing requirement and higher revenue base. The increase in salaries and
related benefits is also attributable to the payroll and related benefits
associated with the increase in comparable unit sales, an increase in the cost
of health insurance provided to employees and paid for in part by us and
increases in employer contributions for other payroll taxes.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restaurant

operating expenses increased $3.0&nbsp;million to $20.1&nbsp;million in 2004
from $17.1&nbsp;million in 2003 (unaudited pro forma). The increase includes $2.0 million that was due to the opening of the
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky units in Dallas, Texas, Houston, Texas and Boston,
Massachusetts. The remaining increase is related to certain costs that are
directly related to the increased sales volume such as credit card charges of
approximately $360,000, increases in property and liability insurance premiums
of approximately $161,000 and professional fees of approximately $281,000 at
the units open the entire period. Restaurant operating expenses as a percentage
of consolidated restaurant sales decreased to 16.3% for 2004 from 16.5%
in 2003.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Occupancy

decreased to 8.8% for 2004 from 10.3% for the 2003 results. General and
administrative expenses include corporate payroll and other expenditures that
benefit both owned and managed units. General and administrative expenses as a

accrual of $525,000 in 2003 for the settlement of a legal action and, to a

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Royalty Expense.</font></i></font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i>Royalty expense increased $364,000 to

due to the increase in sales of $6.5&nbsp;million from our owned Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky units open for the comparable period together with a combined
increase in sales of $11.7&nbsp;million from our Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
unit in Dallas, Texas, which opened in March&nbsp;2003, our unit in Houston,
Texas, which opened in January&nbsp;2004, and our unit in Boston,
Massachusetts, which opened in September&nbsp;2004.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest Expense&#151;Net of
Interest Income.</font></i></font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></i>Interest
expense, net of interest income, increased $546,000 to $1.5 million in 2004
from $965,000 in the 2003 (unaudited pro forma), primarily due to the interest related to the capital lease for the
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky unit in Las Vegas, Nevada and, to a lesser extent,
the interest expense on debt incurred in connection with the financing of our
new Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky units in Dallas, Texas, Houston, Texas, and
Boston, Massachusetts. Interest and other expense, net of interest income, was
also impacted by the reduction in interest income related to the use of cash
for capital improvements, which had been invested in short and long term
interest bearing investments during 2003.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Provision for Income

income tax provisions for 2004 and 2003 (unaudited pro forma) represent certain
state and local taxes.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income of Consolidated

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="RiskRelatedToCertainManagementAgr_121546"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk
Related to Certain Management Agreements</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are subject to various
covenants and operating requirements contained in certain of our management
agreements that, if not complied with or otherwise met, provide for the right
of the other party to terminate these agreements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to management
agreements, we were subject to the right of Plaza Operating Partners to
terminate, at any time, the agreement relating to ONEc.p.s. We were notified by
Plaza Operating Partners during October&nbsp;2004 that it had sold the Plaza
Hotel, the property in which ONEc.p.s, a restaurant we managed, was located. </font>We were directed by the new owners to close
the restaurant by January&nbsp;1, 2005 and to advise the employees of ONEcps of
the closing. On November&nbsp;1, 2004, we informed certain of our employees
that ONEc.p.s. would close effective January&nbsp;1, 2005. As a result,
we no longer accrue additional quarterly management fees under our agreement
with Plaza Operating Partners with respect to any periods following January&nbsp;1,
2005.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pursuant to our lease
agreement for Cit&#233; with Rockefeller Center North,&nbsp;Inc., Rockefeller Center
may terminate the lease agreement if Mr.&nbsp;Stillman does not own at least
35% of the shares of each class of the tenants stock, or if there is a failure
to obtain their consent to an assignment of the lease. We are currently in
default with respect to these requirements, although Rockefeller Center has not
given us notice of default. Rockefeller Center may also terminate the lease
agreement if Mr.&nbsp;Stillman does not have effective working control of the
business of the tenant. The default existing under the lease agreement for Cit&#233;
could subject us to renegotiation of the financial terms of the lease, or could
result in a termination of the lease agreement, which would result in the loss
of the restaurant at this location. This event could have a material adverse
effect on our business and our financial condition and results of operations.
To date, none of the parties to the lease agreement has taken any action to
terminate the agreement and management has no reason to believe that the
agreement will be terminated.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;21, 2005, we received a notice of
default from Rockefeller Center due to our failure to provide Rockefeller
Center with gross income statements for Cit&#233;. We delivered to Rockefeller
Center the requested gross income statements on November&nbsp;15, 2005. No
additional action has been taken by Rockefeller Center.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="HurricaneImpact_104813"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Impairment of Assets
Impacted by Hurricane</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;29, 2005, Hurricane Katrina hit the
Gulf Coast, causing damage to S&amp;W New Orleans. We have insurance policies
that cover certain losses relating to flood and wind damage and coverage for
interruption of business for S&amp;W of New Orleans. We have recorded an impairment
for certain assets of approximately $750,000 which represents an estimate of
the maximum deductible which could be incurred under our insurance plan as well
as an estimate of other impaired assets not believed to&#160; be covered under our insurance plan. This
amount is net of $100,000 of insurance proceeds that we have received to date. We
have also written off approximately $160,000 in inventories that spoiled or
were destroyed by Hurricane Katrina. We received advances of $350,000 for
business interruption which is reflected in our consolidated statement of
operations for the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006. We continue to work closely
with our insurance carriers and claims adjusters to ascertain the full amount
of damages. We are unable to determine when this restaurant will reopen. The failure to reopen our restaurant in New
Orleans in the near future or the failure to collect an adequate amount of
insurance proceeds could have a material adverse effect on our business,
results of operations and financial condition.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="LiquidityAndCapitalResources_104816"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liquidity

the Lease. <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The $1.5 million was used for
construction costs related to the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant in
Boston. The monthly payments were calculated using an annual interest rate of
approximately 7.2%. </font>In connection with the transaction, we entered into
a corporate guaranty on December&nbsp;23, 2004 to guarantee the Lessees&#146;
obligations under the Lease. <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The Lessees may
after 48 months, and after giving 30 days notice, purchase back all the
equipment listed under the Lease at a cost of approximately $405,000.</font></font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The remainder of the fixed
minimum annual rental payments is being treated as an operating lease. See
Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, Notes 12 and 13</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liquidity</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that our cash,
short-term and long-term investments on hand, projected cash flow from
operations and funds available under our Credit Agreement should be sufficient
to finance our redesign of the location where the Manhattan Ocean Club was
located for a new concept, Quality Meats, and maintenance capital expenditures
in respect of existing units and operations throughout 2006, as well as allow
us to meet our debt service obligations under our loan agreements, including
our approximately $1.9&nbsp;million outstanding on our promissory note with
Hibernia, and begin our planned expansion. Our cash resources, and therefore
our liquidity, are dependent upon the level of internally generated cash from
operations. Changes in our operating plans, lower than anticipated sales,
increased expenses or other events could cause us to seek alternative financing
or reschedule our maintenance capital expenditure and expansion plans. While we
would seek to obtain additional funds through commercial borrowings or the
private or public issuance of debt or equity securities, there can be no
assurance that such funds would be available when needed or be available on
terms acceptable to us.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>See &#147;Item 1. Business&#151;Management
Arrangements&#151;Maloney&nbsp;&amp; Porcelli.&#148;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Please refer to the
discussion in the &#147;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#148; section above and the Notes
to Consolidated Financial Statements for additional disclosures regarding these
obligations.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The average interest
rate on long-term debt is approximately 6.7%.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(5)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Payments under capital
lease include the annual fixed rental payments of $21.0 million for the Las
Vegas Property, as well as total principal and interest payments of $1.4
million under the Lease with SBC. See Notes to Consolidated Financial
Statements, Note 12.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(6)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Minimum
annual rental commitments includes annual utility fees of $34,000 required by
the lease of our corporate office.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Seasonality_082929"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Seasonality</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our business is seasonal in nature depending on the
region of the United States in which a particular restaurant is located, with
revenues generally being less in the third quarter than in other quarters due
to reduced summer volume and highest in the fourth quarter due to year-end and
holiday events. As we continue to expand in other locations, the seasonality
pattern may change.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Inflation_082930"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Inflation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Components of our operations subject to inflation
include food, beverage, lease and labor costs. Our leases require us to pay
taxes, maintenance, repairs, insurance, and utilities, all of which are subject
to inflationary increases. We believe inflation has not had a material impact
on our results of operations in recent years.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="EffectOfNewAccountingStandards_082931"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effect of New Accounting Standards</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective October&nbsp;6, 2005, the FASB issued FASB
Staff Position (&#147;FSP&#148;) FAS 13-1, &#147;Accounting for Rental Costs Incurred
during a Construction Period.&#148; The FASB concluded in this FSP that rental costs
associated with&#160; ground or building
operating leases that are incurred during a construction&#160; period be expensed. FASB Technical Bulletin
(FTB) No.&nbsp;88-1,&#148; Issues Relating to Accounting for Leases&#148;, requires
that rental costs associated with&#160;
operating leases be allocated on a straight-line basis in accordance
with </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">52</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='52',FILE='C:\fc\90122613636_D11236_986176\7678-1-da.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 31 12:26 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">FASB&#160; Statement No.&nbsp;13, Accounting&#160; for&#160;
Leases,&#160; and FTB 85-3, Accounting
for Operating Leases with Scheduled Rent Increases, starting with the beginning
of the lease term. The FASB believes there is no distinction between the right
to use a leased asset during the construction period and the right to use that
asset after the construction&#160; period. As
concluded, companies are required to apply the guidance for new leases entered
into from this point on. We had a policy of capitalizing rent during the
construction period and have changed that policy going forward. We do not
believe that the adoption of this FSP will have a material effect on our
consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2005, the FASB issued Statement of
Financial Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No.&nbsp;154, &#147;Accounting Changes and
Error Corrections - a replacement of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;20 and FASB Statement
No.&nbsp;3&#148;. This statement applies to all voluntary changes in accounting
principle and requires retrospective application of the new accounting
principle to prior accounting periods as if that principle had always been used.
In addition, this statement requires that a change in depreciation method be
accounted for as a change in estimate. The requirements are effective for
changes made in fiscal years beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2005. We do not
expect the adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;154 to have a material impact on our
consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;123R,
&#147;Share-Based Payment.&#148; SFAS No.&nbsp;123R revises SFAS No.&nbsp;123, and
generally requires the cost associated with employee services received in
exchange for an award of equity instruments be measured based on the grant-date
fair value of the award and recognized in the financial statements over the
period during which employees are required to provide services in exchange for
the award. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R also provides guidance on how to determine the
grant-date fair value for awards of equity instruments as well as alternative
methods of adopting its requirements. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R is effective for the
beginning of the first annual reporting period after June&nbsp;15, 2005 and
applies to all outstanding and unvested share-based payment awards at a company&#146;s
adoption date. We believe the impact of this statement on our consolidated
financial statements will be comparable to the proforma disclosure.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item7a_QuantitativeAndQualitative_082933"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 7A.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Quantitative
and Qualitative Disclosure About Market Risk.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are exposed to changing interest rates on our
outstanding mortgage in relation to the Smith&nbsp;&amp;&nbsp;Wollensky, Miami
Beach property that bears interest at prime rate plus 1%. The interest cost of
our mortgage is affected by changes in the prime rate. The table below provides
information about our indebtedness that is sensitive to changes in interest
rates as well as our fixed rate of indebtedness. The table presents cash flows
with respect to principal on indebtedness and related weighted average interest
rates by expected maturity dates. Weighted average rates are based on implied
forward rates in the yield curve at January&nbsp;2, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item8_FinancialStatementsAndSuppl_082935"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 8.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Financial
Statements and Supplementary Data.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The information required by this Item 8 is set forth
on pages&nbsp;F-1 to F-41 of this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K
and is hereby incorporated into this Item 8 by reference.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item9_ChangesInAndDisagreementsWi_082936"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 9.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Changes
in and Disagreements With Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Not applicable</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item9a_ControlsAndProcedures__082936"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 9A.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Controls
and Procedures.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="EvaluationOfDisclosureControlsAnd_082936"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Evaluation
of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">An evaluation of the effectiveness of the design and
operation of our &#147;disclosure controls and procedures&#148; (as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;
under the Securities&#160; Exchange Act of
1934, as amended (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;)) as of the end of the period covered by
this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K was made under the supervision and
with the participation of management, including our Chief Executive Officer and
Chief Financial Officer. In&#160; connection
with such evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer
have concluded that our &#147;disclosure controls and procedures&#148; were not effective
based on the restatement described below.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restatement of
Previously Issued Financial Statements</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;20, 2005, it was determined that we had
incorrectly calculated our estimate of gift&#160;
certificates that were sold and deemed to have expired and not redeemed
during fiscal 2001 and fiscal 2002. In addition, it was also determined that we
had not properly recorded expenses related to certain promotions that we ran
from fiscal 2000&#160; through&#160; fiscal&#160;
2004,&#160; for which gift&#160; certificates&#160;
were issued at either a full or partial&#160;
discount. These expenses should have been included in the financial
statements for the fiscal years ended January&nbsp;1, 2001, December&nbsp;31,
2001,&#160; December&nbsp;30, 2002 and December&nbsp;29,
2003, which were included in our Annual&#160;
Report on Form&nbsp;10-K for the fiscal year ended&#160; December&nbsp;29, 2003, and in our
Quarterly&#160; Report on Form&nbsp;10-Q
for the quarterly&#160; periods ended March&nbsp;29,
2004, June&nbsp;28, 2004 and September&nbsp;27, 2004, and therefore a
restatement of our financial statements for the periods&#160; referenced&#160;
above was required. The total impact of this restatement on our
financial statements was to increase our accumulated deficit at December&nbsp;31,
2001 by $590,000, increase our net loss for the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;30,
2002, by $66,000, or $.01 per share, and increase our net loss for the fiscal
year ended December&nbsp;29, 2003 by $83,000, or $.01 per share. We filed a
Report on Form&nbsp;8-K on April&nbsp;26, 2005 describing this
restatement and its impact on our financial statements. This Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K
for the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006 reflects the changes for the
quarterly results for the fiscal year ended 2004. We restated our annual&#160; results for the fiscal years ended&#160; January&nbsp;1, 2001,&#160; December&nbsp;31, 2001, December&nbsp;30,
2002 and&#160; December&nbsp; 29, 2003 in our
Annual&#160; Report on Form&nbsp;10-K
for the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;3, 2005, which was filed on April&nbsp;28,
2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Remediation of
Material Weaknesses</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the first quarter of fiscal 2005, to remedy the
material weakness in our internal control over financial&#160; reporting,&#160;
we established procedures to specifically track every gift certificate
sold and&#160; redeemed&#160; in&#160;
order to recognize any potential expenses and the deferred&#160; revenue in the&#160; appropriate periods. These procedures were
implemented at the beginning of the second quarter of 2005. We are in the
process of monitoring the effectiveness of these controls.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ChangesInInternalControls_082939"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in Internal Controls</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There was no change in our internal controls over
financial reporting (as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;of the
Exchange Act) that occurred during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2005 that has materially&#160; affected, or is&#160; reasonably&#160;
likely to&#160; materially&#160; affect,&#160;
our&#160; internal&#160; controls&#160;
over financial reporting.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name="ReportOfIndependentRegisteredPubl_122322"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting
Firm</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Directors and Stockholders<br>
The Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Restaurant Group,&nbsp;Inc.:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance
sheets of The Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Restaurant Group,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiaries
as of January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 and the related
consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&#146; equity and comprehensive
income (loss) and cash flows for the years then ended. In connection with our
audits of the consolidated financial statements, we also have audited the
financial statement schedule listed in the accompanying index. These
consolidated financial statements and financial statement schedule are the
responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our responsibility is to express an
opinion on these consolidated financial statements and financial statement
schedule based on our audits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the
standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).
Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable
assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material
misstatement. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to
perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. Our audit
included consideration of internal control over financial reporting as a basis
for designing audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but
not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the
Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no
such opinion. An audit also includes examining, on a test basis, evidence
supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing
the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as
well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe
that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our
opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present
fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of The Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky Restaurant Group,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiaries as of January&nbsp;2,
2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 and the results of its operations and its cash
flows for the years then ended, in conformity with accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States. Also in our opinion, the related
financial statement schedule, when considered in relation to the basic
consolidated financial statements taken as a whole, presents fairly, in all
material respects, the information set forth therein.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
fiscal 2004, as required by FASB Interpretation No.&nbsp;46 (R) as discussed in
Note&nbsp;2, the Company has consolidated in the operations of a managed
restaurant that the Company does not own.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><a name="ReportOfIndependentRegisteredPubl_122809"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting
Firm</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Directors and Stockholders<br>
The Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Restaurant Group,&nbsp;Inc.:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated
statements of operations, stockholders&#146; equity and comprehensive income (loss)
and cash flows of The Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Restaurant Group,&nbsp;Inc.
and subsidiaries for the year ended December&nbsp;29, 2003. These consolidated
financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our
responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial
statements based on our audit.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the
standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).
Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable
assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material
misstatement. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used
and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall
financial statement presentation. We believe that our audit provides a
reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements
referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the results of operations
and the cash flows of The Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Restaurant
Group,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiaries for the year ended December&nbsp;29, 2003, in
conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. Also in our
opinion, the related financial statement schedule, when considered in relation
to the basic consolidated financial statements taken as a whole, presents
fairly, in all material respects, the information set forth therein.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As
discussed in Note 23 to the accompanying consolidated financial statements, the
Company has restated the related consolidated statements of operations,
stockholders&#146; equity and comprehensive income (loss), and cash flows for the
year ended December&nbsp;29, 2003 and the accumulated deficit as of December&nbsp;30,
2002.</font></p>

of FIN46(R). See Note 2</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">On May&nbsp;24, 2005, SWRG announced that the Board of
Directors of the Company had authorized a stock repurchase program under which
1.0 million shares of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock were authorized to
be acquired in the open market over the 18 months following such authorization
at the direction of management.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">On August&nbsp;30, 2005, SWRG signed a Separation
Agreement with James M. Dunn, its former President and General Manager of the
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky in Boston. As part of the Seperation Agreement SWRG
agreed to purchase any shares of common stock that Mr.&nbsp;Dunn was to receive
upon the exercise of his stock options at a price of $6.00 per share, less the
exercise price of $3.88 per share. On August&nbsp;30, 2005, SWRG purchased
158,667 shares of common stock from Mr.&nbsp;Dunn. This purchase resulted in a
compensation expense of $336.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;">On November&nbsp;16, 2005, SWRG purchased 41,000 shares
of common stock from Alan M. Mandel, its former Chief Financial Officer. This
resulted in a compensation expense of $72.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 14.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 <br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a1OrganizationAndDescriptionOfBus_125135"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1) Organization
and Description of Business</font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Restaurant Group,&nbsp;Inc.
(formerly The New York Restaurant Group,&nbsp;Inc.) and subsidiaries
(collectively, &#147;SWRG&#148; or the &#147;Company&#148;) operate in a single segment, which
develops, owns, operates and manages a diversified portfolio of upscale
tablecloth restaurants. At January&nbsp;2, 2006, SWRG owned and operated eleven
restaurants, including nine Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants, and managed
three restaurants. In addition, SWRG owns the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky unit
in New Orleans, Louisiana, which was temporarily closed on August&nbsp;29, 2005
due to Hurricane Katrina. At this time, SWRG is unable to determine when this
restaurant will reopen. SWRG also owns its new concept, Quality Meats, a
contemporary American restaurant that is located in the space previously
occupied by the Manhattan Ocean Club and is scheduled to open in the second
quarter of 2006.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG was incorporated in Delaware in October&nbsp;1997.
Prior to October&nbsp;1997, SWRG&#146;s operations were conducted through The New
York Restaurant Group, LLC (&#147;NYRG&#148;) it&#146;s predecessor limited liability company.
During October&nbsp;1997, NYRG merged with SWRG. SWRG completed an initial
public offering (&#147;IPO&#148;) of 5,295,972 shares of common stock in May&nbsp;2001,
of which SWRG sold 4,750,000 shares, at $8.50 per share. Proceeds of the IPO
were used to redeem all of the outstanding debt under SWRG&#146;s senior credit
facility, a $10,000 senior subordinated note and a $1,000 senior revolving
credit facility, including accrued interest and prepayment premiums, and to pay
certain fees and expenses incurred relating to the IPO. All shares of
convertible redeemable preferred stock outstanding automatically converted into
1,448,499 shares of common stock upon the closing of SWRG&#146;s IPO.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;24, 2005, SWRG announced that the Board of
Directors of the Company had authorized a stock repurchase program under which
one million shares of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock were authorized to
be acquired in the open market over the 18 months following such authorization
at the direction of management. &#160;At January&nbsp;2,
2006, SWRG had acquired 927,114 shares of Company common stock that have been
recorded as treasury stock.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a2EffectOfFin46runaudited_123835"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2) Effect of FIN 46(R)&nbsp;(unaudited)</font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with FIN 46(R), SWRG&#146;s consolidated financial
statements for the fiscal years ended January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3,
2005 include the accounts and results of the entity that owns Maloney&nbsp;&amp;
Porcelli (&#147;M&amp;P&#148;). SWRG manages the operations of M&amp;P pursuant to the
terms of a restaurant management agreement (the &#147;Maloney Agreement&#148;). For
comparability purposes, the accounts and results of M&amp;P for the fiscal year
ended December&nbsp;29, 2003 are included on an unaudited pro forma basis in
the table below. FIN 46(R)&nbsp;addresses the consolidation by business enterprises
of variable interest entities. All variable interest entities, regardless of
when created, were required to be evaluated under FIN 46(R)&nbsp;no later than
the first period ending after March&nbsp;15, 2004. An entity shall be subject
to consolidation according to the provisions of FIN 46(R)&nbsp;if, by design,
as a group, the holders of the equity investment at risk lack any one of the
following three characteristics of a controlling financial interest: (1)&nbsp;the
direct or indirect ability to make decisions about an entity&#146;s activities
through voting rights or similar rights; (2)&nbsp;the obligation to absorb the
expected losses of the entity if they occur; or (3)&nbsp;the right to receive
the expected residual returns of the entity if they occur. SWRG consolidated
the accounts and results of the entity that owns M&amp;P because the holders of
the equity investment lacked the right to receive the expected residual returns
of the entity if they were to occur.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the adoption of FIN 46(R), SWRG&#146;s
net investment in the Maloney Agreement, previously classified under &#147;Management
contract, net&#148; and management fees and miscellaneous charges receivable
classified under &#147;Accounts receivable&#148; have been eliminated in consolidation
and, instead, the </font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a3SummaryOfSignificantAccountingP_124147"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3) Summary
of Significant Accounting Policies</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(a) Reporting
Period</font></i></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG
utilizes a 52-or 53-week reporting period ending on the Monday
nearest to December&nbsp;31st. The fiscal year ended January&nbsp;3, 2005
(fiscal 2004) consisted of 53-weeks and the fiscal years ended January&nbsp;2,
2006, (fiscal 2005), and December&nbsp;29, 2003 (fiscal 2003) each consisted of
52-week reporting periods.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(b)&#160; Principles of Consolidation</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of SWRG
after elimination of all material intercompany balances and transactions. </font>In accordance with FIN 46(R), SWRG&#146;s
consolidated financial statements for the fiscal years ended January&nbsp;2,
2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 include the accounts and results of the entity
that owns M&amp;P.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(c)&#160; Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></i></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG
had cash and cash equivalents of $2,362 and&#160;
$1,821 as of January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005, consisting
of cash and overnight repurchase agreements and certificates of deposit with an
initial term of less than three months as of January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3,
2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(d)&#160; Accounts Receivable</font></i></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounts
receivable consists primarily of bank credit card accounts receivable,
management fees receivable and other miscellaneous receivables.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(e)&#160; Allowance for Doubtful Accounts</font></i></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG
estimates an allowance for doubtful accounts based upon the actual payment
history of each individual customer, as well as considering changes that occur
in the financial condition or the local economy of a particular customer that
could affect SWRG&#146;s bad debt expenses and allowance for doubtful accounts. SWRG
performs a specific review of major account balances and applies statistical
experience factors to the various aging categories of receivable balances in
establishing the allowance.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(f)&#160; Inventory</font></i></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Merchandise
inventory consists primarily of restaurant food and beverages and are stated at
the lower of cost or market value. Cost is determined using the first-in,
first-out method.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(g)&#160; Investment Securities</font></i></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investment
securities at January&nbsp;2, 2006 consist of debt and equity securities. Investment
securities at January&nbsp;3, 2005 consist of equity securities. SWRG
classifies its debt and equity securities as available for sale securities. The
securities are recorded at fair value. Unrealized holding gains and losses, net
of the related tax effect, on available for sale securities are excluded from
earnings and are reported as &#145;accumulated other comprehensive income&#146; as a
separate component of stockholder&#146;s equity until realized. There were no
material unrealized holding gains or losses as of January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3,
2005. Realized gains and losses from the sale of available for sale securities
are determined on a specific identification basis.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">10</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A
decline in the market value of any available for sale security below cost that
is deemed to be other than temporary results in a reduction in carrying amount
to fair value. The impairment is charged to earnings and a new cost basis for
the security is established. To determine whether an impairment is other than
temporary, SWRG considers whether it has the ability and intent to hold the
investment until a market price recovery and considers whether evidence
indicating the cost of the investment is recoverable outweighs evidence to the
contrary. Evidence considered in this assessment includes the reasons for the
impairment, changes in value subsequent to year-end and forecasted performance
of the investee.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Premiums
and discounts are amortized or accreted over the life of the related available
for sale security as an adjustment to yield using the effective interest
method. Dividend and interest income are recognized when earned.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(h) Property and Equipment</font></i></b></p>

<p style="line-height:11.9pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property and equipment is
stated at cost. Landlord allowances for leasehold improvements, furniture,
fixtures and equipment are recorded as a liability and amortized as a reduction
of rent expense. Depreciation is calculated on a straight-line basis over the
estimated useful lives of the assets. Leasehold improvements and rights are
amortized on the straight-line basis over the shorter of the lease term
(assuming renewal options) or the estimated useful life of the asset. Any rent
expense incurred during the construction period was capitalized as a part of
leasehold improvements and is amortized on a straight-line basis from the date
operations commence over the remaining life of the lease, which includes the
renewal period. For any leases entered into after September&nbsp;15, 2005, SWRG
will be expensing these costs in conjunction with FASB Staff Position FAS 13-1,
&#147;Accounting for Rental Costs Incurred during a Construction Period&#148;. The
estimated useful lives are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(i)&#160; Artwork</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG purchases artwork and
antiques for display in its restaurants. SWRG does not depreciate artwork and
antiques since these assets have cultural, aesthetic or historical value that
is worth preserving perpetually and SWRG has the ability and intent to protect
and preserve these assets. Such assets are recorded at cost and are included in
other assets in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(j)&#160;&#160; Goodwill</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill represents the
excess of fair value of the aggregate of certain reporting units acquired in
the formation of SWRG over the aggregate book value of identifiable net assets
for those reporting units. SWRG adopted the provisions of the Statement of
Financial Accounting Standards No.&nbsp;142, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Goodwill and
Other Intangible Assets </font></i>(&#147;SFAS No.&nbsp;142&#148;)<i><font style="font-style:italic;">,</font></i>
as of January&nbsp;1, 2002. Goodwill and intangible assets determined to have
an indefinite life are not subject to amortization but are tested at least
annually for impairment in accordance with the provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;142.
An impairment loss is recognized to the extent that the </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">11</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-11',FILE='C:\fc\8920531246_CX93V61_981347\7678-1-fm.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 30 20:05 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">implied
fair value of the aggregate of certain reporting units is less than their
aggregate carrying amount. SFAS No.&nbsp;142 also requires that intangible
assets with estimable useful lives be amortized over their respective estimated
useful lives to their estimated residual values, and reviewed for impairment.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with SFAS No.&nbsp;142&#146;s
transitional goodwill impairment evaluation, the statement required SWRG to
perform an assessment of whether there was an indication that goodwill is
impaired as of the date of adoption. Upon adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;142, SWRG
had originally identified its reporting units by restaurant and their carrying
values by assigning the assets and liabilities, including the existing goodwill
and intangible assets, to those reporting units as of January&nbsp;1, 2002. </font>In September&nbsp;2004, the Emerging Issues
Task Force (&#147;EITF&#148;) reached a consensus on EITF Issue 04-10 <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Applying Paragraph 19 of FASB Statement No.&nbsp;131,
&#147;Disclosures about Segments of an Enterprise and Related Information&#148; (&#147;FASB No.&nbsp;131&#148;)
in Determining Whether to Aggregate Operating Segments that do not meet the
Quantitative Thresholds</font></i>. The consensus concluded that operating
segments that do not meet certain quantitative thresholds can be aggregated if
the criteria set forth in paragraph 17 of FASB No.&nbsp;131 is met. As a result
of the consensus reached in September&nbsp;2004 by the EITF in regard to
determining whether to aggregate operating segments of an enterprise, SWRG
concluded that the entities that were previously viewed as separate reporting
entities could now be viewed as one single reporting entity for purposes of
assessing goodwill. As such, starting in fiscal 2004, SWRG compares the fair
value of the single reporting entity, using the discounted cash flows method,
to the total equity (carrying value) to determine if an impairment exists.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For fiscal 2005, the fair
value of the single reporting unit is in excess of the recorded carrying value.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(k)&#160; Long-Lived
Assets</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;144,
long-lived assets, such as property, plant, and equipment, and purchased
intangibles subject to amortization, are reviewed for impairment on a
restaurant-by-restaurant basis whenever events or changes in circumstances
indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable.
Recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the
carrying amount of an asset to the estimated undiscounted future cash flows
expected to be generated by the asset. If the carrying amount of an asset
exceeds its estimated future cash flows, an impairment charge is recognized by
the amount by which the carrying amount of the asset exceeds the fair value of
the asset. SWRG recorded an impairment of $750, net of insurance proceeds for
the assets of its Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky in New Orleans, which were damaged
by Hurricane Katrina during the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006. SWRG also
recorded a write down of $314 for the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006 for the
assets of the Manhattan Ocean Club, a restaurant that was closed on
December&nbsp;31, 2005 and is being renovated into a new concept. Assets to be
disposed of would be separately presented in the balance sheet and reported at
the lower of the carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell, and are no
longer depreciated. The assets and liabilities of a disposed group classified
as held for sale would be presented separately in the appropriate asset and
liability sections of the balance sheet.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Costs attributable to a
sale and licensing agreement (the &#147;Licensing Agreement&#148;) entered into in 1996
consisted of a $2,500 payment (plus any payments made upon the opening of
additional units) and legal fees paid by SWRG to acquire the rights and license
to use the names &#147;Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky&#148; and &#147;Wollensky&#146;s Grill&#148;
(collectively, the &#147;Names&#148;) as described in Note&nbsp;7. The Licensing
Agreement exists in perpetuity and the original $2,500 payment is being
amortized over the thirty year estimated useful life of </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">12</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-12',FILE='C:\fc\8920531246_CX93V61_981347\7678-1-fm.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 30 20:05 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the
Names, using the straight-line method. Any payments made upon the opening of
additional units are being amortized over the lesser of the life of the lease,
including the renewal period, or the remaining useful life of the Names, using
the straight-line method. The net balance as of January&nbsp;2, 2006 was
$3,471.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of the
acquisition of the management contract for the Maloney&nbsp;&amp; Porcelli
restaurant in New York City amounting to $1,500 was being amortized over the
fifteen-year period of the underlying operating lease, using the straight-line
method. </font>In connection
with the adoption of FIN46 (R)&nbsp;during the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;3,
2005, the $1,500 and related accumulated amortization were eliminated in the
consolidation of Maloney&nbsp;&amp; Porcelli.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of the
acquisition of the management contract for the ONEc.p.s. restaurant amounted to
$500 in 2000 and was being amortized over the ten year period of the underlying
management contract, using the straight-line method. The accumulated
amortization as of December&nbsp;31, 2001 was $65. In September&nbsp;2002, SWRG
determined that the carrying amount of the management contract and receivable
from the ONEc.p.s. restaurant was not recoverable and an impairment had
occurred. SWRG recorded a charge for investment in managed restaurants of $722
in the third quarter of 2002, which consisted of a $398 charge against the net
investment in the management contract and a $324 charge against the receivable.
SWRG was notified by Plaza Operating Partners during October&nbsp;2004 that it
sold the Plaza Hotel, the property in which ONEc.p.s, a restaurant SWRG
managed, was located. </font>SWRG
was directed by the new owners to close the restaurant by January&nbsp;1, 2005
and to advise the employees of ONEcps of the closing. On November&nbsp;1, 2004,
SWRG informed certain of its employees that ONEc.p.s. would close effective January&nbsp;1,
2005. As a result, SWRG no longer accrues additional quarterly
management fees under its agreement with Plaza Operating Partners with respect
to any periods following January&nbsp;1, 2005.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Amortization expense of
intangible assets aggregated $176, $185 and $351 in fiscal 2005, 2004 and 2003,
respectively, and is included in general and administrative expenses in the accompanying
consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(l)&#160;&#160; Deferred
Rent</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG records rental
expense on a straight-line basis from the date that SWRG takes control of the
premises over the lease term, including renewal periods. Any difference between
the calculated expense and the amounts actually paid are reflected as a
deferred rent liability in the consolidated balance sheets. SWRG also includes
in deferred rent liability landlord allowances for leasehold improvements,
furniture, fixtures and equipment. These amounts are amortized on a
straight-line basis from the date that SWRG takes control of the premise over
the lease term, including renewal periods. Any rent expense incurred during the
construction period was capitalized as a part of leasehold improvements and is
amortized on a straight-line basis from the date operations commence over the
remaining life of the lease, which includes the renewal period. Starting in the
first reporting period after September&nbsp;15, 2005, SWRG will be expensing
these costs in conjunction with FASB Staff Position FAS 13-1, &#147;Accounting
for Rental Costs Incurred during a Construction Period&#148;.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(m)&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
Marketing and Promotional Expenses</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Marketing and promotional
expenses in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations include advertising
expenses of&#160; $1,860, $2,289 and $1,323
for fiscal 2005, 2004, and 2003, respectively. Marketing and promotional costs
are recorded as expense over the period receiving the promotional benefit
within the fiscal year.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(n) Pre-Opening
Costs</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pre-opening costs incurred
in connection with the opening of new restaurants are expensed as incurred and
are included in general and administrative expenses in the accompanying
consolidated statements of operations.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(o)&#160; Debt
Financing Costs</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred debt financing
costs, which were included in other assets (see Note&nbsp;9), relate to costs
incurred in connection with bank borrowings and other long-term debt and are
amortized over the term of the related borrowings. Amortization expense of
deferred financing costs was $ 61, $112 and $59 in fiscal 2005, 2004 and&#160; 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(p)&#160; Income
Taxes</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Income taxes are accounted
for under the asset and liability method. Deferred tax assets and liabilities
are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences
between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and
liabilities and their respective tax bases. Deferred tax assets and liabilities
are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the
years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or
settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax
rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(q)&#160; Stock Option
Plan</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG applies the intrinsic
value-based method of accounting prescribed by Accounting Principles
Board (&#147;APB&#148;) Opinion No.&nbsp;25, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock
Issued to Employees</font></i>, and related interpretations including FASB
Interpretation No.&nbsp;44, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Certain
Transactions involving Stock Compensation an interpretation of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;25</font></i>
issued in March&nbsp;2000 (&#147;FIN 44&#148;), to account for its fixed plan stock
options. Under this method, compensation expense is recorded on the date of
grant only if the current market price of the underlying stock exceeded the
exercise price. Statement of Financial Accounting Standard (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No.&nbsp;123,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation</font></i>,
established accounting and disclosure requirements using a fair value-based
method of accounting for stock-based employee compensation plans. In December&nbsp;2002,
the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;148, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock-Based
Compensation Transition and Disclosure, an amendment of FASB Statement No.&nbsp;123</font></i>.
This Statement amends FASB Statement No.&nbsp;123, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting
for Stock-Based Compensation</font></i>, to provide alternative methods
of transition for a voluntary change to the fair value method of accounting for
stock-based employee compensation. SWRG has adopted the pro forma
disclosure requirements of SFAS No.&nbsp;123, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting
for Stock-Based Compensation</font></i>. Options given to a board member
who was also a consultant of SWRG became variable options under FIN 44. SWRG
took an&#160; initial&#160; non-cash&#160;
compensation&#160; charge and will
continue to record such charges, or revenues, associated with the change in
fair value of the stock&#160; underlying these
options through the earlier of their exercise,&#160;
forfeiture or expiration&#160; dates.
The change in fair value of these options resulted in an immaterial
compensation expense for the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006 and a
compensation expense of $50 for the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;2, 2005.</font></p>
