<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Includes </font>the accounts and results of the entity that owns M&amp;P
as a direct result of<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;"> the adoption of
FIN46(R). See Note 2</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The per share
weighted-average fair value of stock options granted from fiscal 2001 to fiscal
2005 range from $1.77 to $3.45 on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes
option pricing model with the following weighted average assumptions: expected
dividend yield of 0%, risk free rate ranging from 3.9% to 4.9%, expected stock
volatility ranging from 32% to 50% and an expected life ranging from five to
seven years.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(r)&#160; Use of
Estimates</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation of the
consolidated financial statements in conformity with generally accepted
accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions
that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of
contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and
the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting period.
Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(s)&#160; Fair
Value of Financial Instruments</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying value of SWRG&#146;s
accounts receivable and accounts payable approximate their fair values based on
the short-term nature of such items. The carrying value of the mortgage
included in long-term debt approximates fair value since the interest rate is
variable at terms currently available to SWRG. The fair value of the term loans
and promissory notes was estimated using a discounted cash flow analysis based
on SWRG&#146;s incremental borrowing rate. The fair value of the term loans and
promissory note at January&nbsp;2, </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:12.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">15</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2006 was
approximately $3,640. Fair value of investments is determined by the most
recently traded price of each security at the balance sheet date. Net realized
gains or losses are determined on the specific identification cost method.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(t)&#160; Revenue Recognition</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Sales from consolidated
restaurants are recognized as revenue at the point of the delivery of meals and
services. Management fee income is recognized as the related management fee is
earned, pursuant to the respective agreements.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(u) Gift Certificate Liability</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We record a gift
certificate liability for gift certificates sold to customers to be redeemed at
a future date. The liability is relieved and revenue is recognized when the
gift certificates are redeemed.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(v)&#160; Concentration
of Credit Risk</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial instruments
which potentially subject SWRG to concentration of credit risks consist
principally of cash and accounts receivable. SWRG maintains its cash in
commercial banks insured by the FDIC. At times, such cash in banks exceeds the
FDIC insurance limit. SWRG has established as allowance for doubtful accounts
based upon factors surrounding the credit risk of special customers, historical
trends and other information.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt 20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(w) Effect of
New Accounting Standards</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective October&nbsp;6,
2005, the FASB issued FASB Staff Position (&#147;FSP&#148;) FAS 13-1, &#147;Accounting
for Rental Costs Incurred during a Construction Period.&#148; The FASB concluded in
this FSP that rental costs associated with ground or building operating leases
that are incurred during a construction period be expensed. FASB Technical
Bulletin (FTB) No.&nbsp;88-1,&#148;Issues Relating to Accounting for Leases&#148;,
requires that rental costs&#160;
associated&#160; with&#160; operating leases be allocated on a&#160; straight-line basis in accordance with FASB
Statement No.&nbsp;13, Accounting&#160; for
Leases, and FTB 85-3, Accounting for Operating Leases with Scheduled Rent
Increases, starting with the beginning of the lease term. The FASB believes
there is no distinction between the right to use a leased asset during the
construction period and the right to use that asset after the construction
period. As concluded, companies are required to apply the guidance for new
leases entered into from this point on. SWRG had a policy of capitalizing rent
during the construction period and as of the adoption of this FSP has changed
that policy for future leases. SWRG&#146;s current policy is to expense rent during
the construction period. SWRG does not believe that the adoption of this FSP
will have a material effect on our consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2005, the FASB
issued Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No.&nbsp;154, &#147;Accounting&#160; Changes and Error Corrections - a replacement
of APB Opinion No.&nbsp;20 and FASB&#160;
Statement&#160; No.&nbsp;3&#148;. This
statement applies to all voluntary changes in accounting principle and requires
retrospective application of the new accounting principle to prior accounting
periods as if that principle had always been used. In addition, this statement
requires that a change in depreciation method be accounted for as a change in
estimate. The requirements are effective for changes made in fiscal years
beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2005. SWRG does&#160; not expect the adoption of SFAS No.&nbsp;154
to have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004, the
FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;123R, &#147;Share-Based Payment.&#148; SFAS No.&nbsp;123R
revises SFAS No.&nbsp;123, and generally requires the cost associated with
employee services received in exchange for an award of equity instruments be
measured based on the grant-date fair value of the award and recognized in the
financial statements over the period during which employees are required to
provide services in exchange for the award. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R also provides
guidance on how to determine the grant-date fair value for awards of equity instruments
as well as alternative methods of adopting its requirements. SFAS No.&nbsp;123R
is effective for the beginning of the first annual reporting period after June&nbsp;15,
2005 and applies to all outstanding and unvested share-based payment awards at
a company&#146;s adoption date. SWRG believes the impact of this statement on our
consolidated financial statements will be comparable to the proforma
disclosure.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">(x)&#160; Reclassifications</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain reclassifications
have been made to the prior period consolidated financial statements to conform
them to current presentation.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a4NetLossPerCommonShare_130621"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4) Net Loss Per
Common Share</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG calculates earnings
(loss) per common share in accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;128, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Earnings Per Share</font></i>. Basic earnings (loss) per common share
are computed by dividing the net loss applicable to common shares by the
weighted average number of common shares outstanding. Diluted earnings (loss)
per common share assumes the conversion of the convertible redeemable preferred
shares as of the beginning of the year and the exercise of stock options and
warrants using the treasury stock method, if dilutive. Dilutive net loss per
common share for fiscal 2005, fiscal 2004 and fiscal 2003 are the same as basic
net loss per common share due to the antidilutive effect of the exercise of stock
options. Such options amounted to 322,023, 449,223 and 326,153 for fiscal 2005,
fiscal 2004 and fiscal 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Includes </font>the accounts and results of the
entity that owns M&amp;P as a direct result of<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">
the adoption of FIN46(R). See Note 2</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On
May&nbsp;24, 2005, SWRG announced that the Board of Directors of the Company
had authorized a stock repurchase program under which 1.0 million shares of the
Company&#146;s outstanding common stock were authorized to be acquired in the open
market over the 18 months following such authorization at the direction of
management.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On
August&nbsp;30, 2005, SWRG signed a Separation Agreement with James M. Dunn,
the former President and General Manager of the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky in
Boston. As part of the Separation Agreement,&#160;
SWRG agreed to purchase any shares of common stock that Mr.&nbsp;Dunn
was to receive upon the exercise of his stock options at a price of $6.00 per
share, less the exercise price of $3.88 per share. On August&nbsp;30, 2005,
SWRG purchased 158,667 shares of common stock from Mr.&nbsp;Dunn. This purchase
resulted in a compensation expense of $336.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On
November&nbsp;16, 2005, SWRG purchased 41,000 shares of common stock from Alan
M. Mandel, its former Chief Financial Officer. This resulted in a compensation
expense of $72.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 40.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Dilutive
shares and basic shares are the same due to the antidilutive effect of the
exercise of stock options.</p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Leasehold improvements include $6,564 of assets under
capital lease and machinery and equipment includes $1,500 of assets under
capital lease as of January&nbsp;2, 2006. Included in land at January&nbsp;3,
2005 was $8,044 of assets under capital lease that were sold on May&nbsp;23,
2005 (see Note 12). Depreciation and amortization expense of property and
equipment was $5,036, $4,509 and $3,868 in fiscal 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.
SWRG capitalizes interest cost as a component of the cost of construction in
progress. In connection with SWRG&#146;s assets under construction in 2004 SWRG
capitalized $123 of interest costs in accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;34, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Capitalization of Interest Cost</font></i>. There was no interest
capitalized in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;29, 2005 SWRG closed its Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky in New Orleans due to damages that it sustained from Hurricane
Katrina. SWRG has a write-down of the impaired net property and equipment of $750,
net for the estimated damages to the building. This estimate is net of $100 of
insurance proceeds SWRG has received related to content coverage but does not
reflect any potential future insurance recovery. SWRG is currently unable to
determine when or if it will receive any additional insurance proceeds. At this
time, SWRG is unable to determine when it&#146;s restaurant in New Orleans will
reopen and SWRG is currently evaluating its options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;1, 2006
SWRG closed the Manhattan Ocean Club and began renovations for its new concept,
Quality Meats, expected to open in the second quarter of 2006. The write-down
of the impaired net property and equipment of MOC was approximately $302 for
the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a7LicensingAgreement_133549"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(7) Licensing Agreement</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;16, 1996, SWRG entered into a Licensing
Agreement with St. James Associates (&#147;St.&nbsp;James&#148;), the owner of the Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky restaurant in New York. St. James is an entity related through common
management and ownership (see Note&nbsp;19).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Licensing Agreement provides SWRG with the
exclusive right to utilize the Names throughout the United States and
internationally, with the exception of a reserved territory, as defined. Consequently,
SWRG may not open additional Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurants or
otherwise utilize the Names in the reserved territory. The Licensing Agreement
requires SWRG to make additional payments to St. James as </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">20</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p> <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">follows: (i)&nbsp;$200 for
each new restaurant opened (increasing annually commencing in 1999 by the
lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or a 5% increase of
the fee required in the preceding year), (ii)&nbsp;a royalty fee of 2% based
upon annual gross sales for each restaurant utilizing the Names, as defined,
subject to certain annual minimums, and (iii)&nbsp;a royalty fee of 1% of
annual gross sales for any steakhouses opened in the future by SWRG that does
not utilize the Names. In addition, should SWRG terminate or default on the
license, as defined, it is subject to a fee of $2,000 upon termination or
$2,500 to be paid over four years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;19, 2006, SWRG (the &#147;Licensee&#148;),
signed an Amended and Restated Sale and License Agreement, dated as of January&nbsp;1,
2006 (the &#147;Amended Licensing Agreement&#148;), with St. James Associates, L.P. (the &#147;Licensor&#148;),
which provides for, among other things, a reduced licensing fee only for the
opening of Grills that are less than 9,000 square feet. Pursuant to the Amended
Licensing Agreement, the one-time opening fee paid to the Licensee for each new
additional Wollensky&#146;s Grill (&#147;Grill Opening Fee&#148;) will be at a rate equal to
50% of the fee due under the original licensing agreement. In addition, the
annual royalty fee (&#147;Grill Royalty Fee&#148;) will be reduced from 2% to 1% for
annual sales from Wollensky&#146;s Grills. Both the Grill Opening Fee and Grill
Royalty Fee are subject to maximum average per-person checks that, if exceeded,
could increase both the Grill Opening Fee and Grill Royalty Fee, but not to
exceed the opening fee and royalty fee contained in the original licensing
agreement. The terms of the amendment do not apply to the existing Wollensky&#146;s
Grills.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior to December&nbsp;2002, SWRG operated Park Avenue
Caf&#233; in Chicago, Mrs.&nbsp;Park&#146;s Tavern and the other services of the food and
beverage department of the Doubletree Hotel in Chicago (&#147;Doubletree&#148;) pursuant
to a sub-management agreement (the &#147;Doubletree Agreement&#148;). SWRG received a
management fee equal to the sum of 1.5% of sales and a percentage of earnings,
as defined. The Doubletree Agreement was to expire on the earlier of December&nbsp;31,
2004 or the termination of the related hotel management agreement between
Chicago HSR Limited Partnership (&#147;HSR&#148;), the owner of the Doubletree and
Doubletree Partners, the manager of the Doubletree. During December&nbsp;2002,
HSR closed the Park Avenue Caf&#233; restaurant in Chicago and discontinued SWRG&#146;s
requirement to provide other food and beverage department service for the
Doubletree. As a result, SWRG no longer receives the fees described above.
During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2003, SWRG reached an
agreement with HSR. The agreement provides for the continued use by HSR of the
name Mrs.&nbsp;Parks Tavern and requires SWRG to provide management services to
support that location. In exchange for the use of the Mrs.&nbsp;Park&#146;s Tavern
name and related management support SWRG received an annual fee of $50. The
agreement was to automatically renew each year, unless notification of
cancellation is given, by either party, at least 90&nbsp;days prior to December&nbsp;31.
The change in this agreement resulted in a lower than anticipated future cash
flow for SWRG under the terms of the Doubletree Agreement. The change required
SWRG to reassess the fair value of its goodwill, which resulted in an
impairment charge of $75. During 2004, SWRG agreed to reduce its annual fee to
$12 for the continued use by HSR of the name Mrs.&nbsp;Parks Tavern, but no
longer provides management services to support the location.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG managed the operations of the ONEc.p.s.
restaurant, located in the Plaza Hotel, New York, pursuant to the terms of a
restaurant management agreement between Plaza Operating Partners,&nbsp;Ltd. (&#147;Owner&#148;)
and Parade 59 Restaurant, LLC (&#147;Manager&#148;), an entity SWRG controls, dated September&nbsp;7,
2000 (the &#147;ONEc.p.s. Agreement&#148;). SWRG paid $500 for the right to provide these
management services. </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">22</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-22',FILE='C:\fc\9313220209_F25892_993383\7678-1-fq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Apr  3 13:22 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p> <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the provisions of
the ONEc.p.s. Agreement, SWRG was to receive a management fee equal to the sum
of 4% of the gross revenues recognized from services provided at ONEc.p.s plus
an additional fee, as set forth in the ONEc.p.s. agreement. The ONEc.p.s.
Agreement would have expired on September&nbsp;12, 2010 and could have been
terminated by the restaurant owner (i)&nbsp;if SWRG failed to meet the
agreement&#146;s performance goals, (ii)&nbsp;at any time, upon 90&nbsp;days&#146; notice
to SWRG and the payment of a fee, determined by a formula in the ONEc.p.s.
Agreement, which allows for a maximum payment to SWRG of four years of
additional management fees or (iii)&nbsp;at any time, if the person who
controls SWRG&#146;s day-to-day operations or has overall control and decision
making authority, is replaced by means other than in the ordinary course of
SWRG&#146;s business operations. The ONEc.p.s. Agreement could have been terminated
by Plaza Operating Partners,&nbsp;Ltd. at any time immediately upon notice to
us, due to the fact that pre-opening costs, as defined, exceeded $5,250.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of September&nbsp;30, 2002, SWRG had contributed
$500 for the right to provide management services for the ONEc.p.s restaurant
and had contributed, since the restaurants inception in September&nbsp;2000,
approximately $924 of additional funding for this restaurant. Under the terms
of the agreement, SWRG was to be repaid for the additional funding they had
provided. SWRG recorded a reserve of $300 in 2001 based on its determination
that, at the time, part of the receivable might not be recoverable. During the
third quarter ended September&nbsp;30, 2002, SWRG determined that the carrying
value of the management contract was impaired and the remaining investment of
$398 was written off. In the fourth quarter of 2002, SWRG reached an agreement
with Plaza Operating Partners,&nbsp;Ltd. in October&nbsp;2002 and collected
$300 as its share of the additional funding for operating losses. During the
three months ended September&nbsp;30, 2002, SWRG recorded an additional
write-off of $324 for the remaining portion of the receivable.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;31, 2003, SWRG and Manager, amended
the ONEc.p.s. Agreement with Owner. Effective January&nbsp;1, 2004, Owner
agreed to pay Manager $50 per quarter as a minimum base management fee. The
minimum base management fee was to be credited against any management fee that
Manager earned under the ONEc.p.s Agreement. This amendment also gave either
party the right to fund or refuse to fund any necessary working capital
requirements. Plaza Operating Partners agreed to fund the cash requirements of
ONEc.p.s. until October&nbsp;16, 2004, the date that SWRG was notified that the
Plaza Hotel was sold, the property in which ONEc.p.s was located, </font>and the date the Plaza Operating Partners
directed us to advise the employees of ONEc.p.s. of the closing. SWRG
funded the cash requirements of ONEc.p.s. until January&nbsp;1, 2005 the date on which we were required to close
the restaurant at the direction of the new owner. On November&nbsp;1, 2004,
SWRG informed certain of its employees that ONEc.p.s. would close effective January&nbsp;1,
2005. As a result, SWRG no longer accrues additional quarterly
management fees under its agreement with Plaza Operating Partners with respect
to any periods following January&nbsp;1, 2005.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;22, 2004, Parade 59 Restaurant, LLC (&#147;Parade&#148;),
a wholly owned subsidiary of SWRG that managed the ONEc.p.s. restaurant in the
Plaza Hotel,&#160; filed suit against&#160; Plaza Operating Partners, Ltd, ELAD&#160;&#160; Properties NY, LLC and CPS1 Realty, LP
(collectively the &#147;Defendants&#148;) alleging that the Defendants (1)&nbsp;failed to
pay a base management fee to Parade as provided for in the restaurant
management agreement described above, (2)&nbsp;failed to pay hotel, guest, room
and credit account charges to Parade, and (3)&nbsp;failed to pay termination
obligations to Parade in connection with the termination of the restaurant
management agreement. On February&nbsp;28, 2005, the Defendants served their
answers and counterclaims against Parade alleging, among other things, that
Parade (1)&nbsp;failed to make payments, </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">23</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-23',FILE='C:\fc\9313220209_F25892_993383\7678-1-fq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Apr  3 13:22 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p> <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)&nbsp;breached a&#160; memorandum of understanding and other
agreements and (3)&nbsp;is liable for attorney fees and costs, with damages
totaling no less than $3,500. CPS1 Realty, LP and ELAD Properties NY, LLC (the &#147;CPS
1 Defendants&#148;) subsequently served an amended answer with counterclaims on May&nbsp;16,
2005 adding a counterclaim for a declaratory judgment that the management
agreement was terminated as a result of Parade&#146;s default under the management
agreement. On September&nbsp;30, 2005, the CPS1 Defendants served a motion for
summary judgment seeking judgment on their claim that the management agreement
was terminated as a result of Parade&#146;s default. SWRG believes that it will
likely prevail in the counterclaims and that the risk of material loss is not
probable. Accordingly, SWRG has not established a reserve for loss in
connection with the counterclaims. If Parade were to lose the counterclaims,
SWRG&#146;s financial position, results of operations and cash flows could be
adversely affected.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG is subject to various
covenants and operating requirements in these management agreements that, if
not complied with or otherwise met, provide for the right of the other party to
terminate these agreements. SWRG was in compliance with the above at January&nbsp;2,
2006.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>In fiscal 1997, SWRG
assumed certain liabilities in connection with the acquisition of leasehold
rights relating to its Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky Miami Beach location from two
bankrupt corporations. Pursuant to the terms of the bankruptcy resolution, SWRG
was obligated to make quarterly and annual payments over a six-year period.
These obligations generally bore interest at rates ranging from 9% to 12%. The
final payment for these obligations was made in 2003. In addition, SWRG assumed
a mortgage on the property that requires monthly payments and bears interest at
prime rate plus 1%. On April&nbsp;30, 2004, </p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p> <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">a letter was signed by the
financial institution that holds the mortgage for the property extending the
term of the mortgage three additional years, with the final principal payment
due in June&nbsp;2007. The extension became effective June&nbsp;2004. In fiscal
1997, SWRG also assumed a loan payable to a financing institution that requires
monthly payments through 2014, and bears interest at a fixed rate of 7.67% per
year.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(b)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On August&nbsp;23, 2002,
SWRG entered into a $14.0&nbsp;million secured term loan agreement with Morgan
Stanley Dean Witter Commercial Financial Services,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Morgan Stanley&#148;).
Under the agreement, SWRG is the guarantor of borrowings by its wholly owned
subsidiary, S&amp;W Las Vegas, LLC (the &#147;Borrower&#148;). SWRG, through the
Borrower, borrowed $4.0&nbsp;million under the agreement for general corporate
purposes, including its new restaurant development program. This portion of the
loan bears interest at a fixed rate of 6.35% per annum. Principal payments for
this portion of the loan commenced June&nbsp;30, 2003. Pursuant to the terms of
the loan agreement, SWRG is obligated to make monthly principal payments of
approximately $33 for this portion of the loan over the term of the loan and a
balloon payment of approximately $2,033 on May&nbsp;31, 2008, the maturity date
of the loan. The term loan is secured by a leasehold mortgage relating to the
Las Vegas property and all of the personal property and fixtures of the
Borrower. As previously disclosed, the balance of the funds available under the
agreement had been intended to be used by SWRG to exercise its purchase option
for the land and building at 3767 Las Vegas Blvd. where SWRG operates its 675-seat,
30,000 square foot restaurant. The ability to draw down this balance expired on
May&nbsp;31, 2003. SWRG did not draw down the remaining balance because, as an
alternative to purchasing the land, SWRG signed an amendment to its lease
agreement, as discussed below. In connection with the transaction involving the
Las Vegas property described in Note 13 below, the remaining balance
outstanding on this secured term loan of $3,233, including accrued interest was
repaid on May&nbsp;23, 2005.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(c)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On October&nbsp;9,
2002, SWRG purchased the property for the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky unit in
Dallas. The purchase price for this property was $3.75&nbsp;million. A portion
of the purchase price for this property was financed through a
$1.65&nbsp;million promissory note that was signed by Dallas S&amp;W, L.P., a
wholly owned subsidiary of SWRG and issued to Toll Road Texas Land Company,
L.P. This loan bears interest at 8% per annum and requires annual principal
payments of $550 with the first installment being prepaid on March&nbsp;4,
2003, and the subsequent two installments originally due on October&nbsp;9,
2004 and October&nbsp;9, 2005, respectively. SWRG received a 60-day extension
on the installment due on October&nbsp;9, 2004, which SWRG paid on December&nbsp;9,
2004. The promissory note is secured by a first mortgage relating to the Dallas
property. The final installment of this promissory note, including accrued
interest of $572, was prepaid, with no prepayment penalty, on June&nbsp;15,
2005.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(d)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On December&nbsp;24,

Morgan Stanley. Under the agreement, SWRG and Dallas S&amp;W L.P., a wholly
owned subsidiary of SWRG, are the guarantors of borrowings by the Borrower. Of
the $1.9&nbsp;million borrowed by SWRG, through the Borrower, under the
agreement, $1.35&nbsp;million was used for its new restaurant development
program, and $550 was used for the first principal installment on the
$1.65&nbsp;million promissory note with Toll Road Texas Land Company, L.P.
described above in note 11(c). This loan bears interest at a fixed rate of
6.36% per annum. Principal payments for this loan commenced January&nbsp;24,
2003. Pursuant to the terms of the loan agreement, SWRG is obligated to make
monthly principal payments </p>

2007, the maturity date of the loan. The term loan is secured by a second

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(e)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On January&nbsp;30,
2004, SWRG entered into a $2.0&nbsp;million secured line of credit facility
with Morgan Stanley. Under the agreement, SWRG is the guarantor of borrowings
by the Borrower. Through the Borrower, SWRG has the ability to borrow up to
$2.0&nbsp;million under the agreement for working capital purposes. Advances
under this line of credit will bear interest at a fixed rate of LIBOR, which
was 2.4% at December&nbsp;31, 2004, plus 3% per annum, payable on a monthly
basis. SWRG is also subject to an unused availability fee of 1.75% for any
unused portion of this line, payable on a quarterly basis. SWRG may at anytime
repay advances on this line without penalty. SWRG is obligated to repay the
principal portion of this line on January&nbsp;30, 2006, the termination date
of this line. This line is secured by a leasehold mortgage relating to the Las
Vegas property and all of the personal property and fixtures of the Borrower. In
connection with the transaction involving the Las Vegas property described in
Note 9 below, the remaining balance outstanding on this secured line of credit
facility of $2,000, including accrued interest, was repaid on May&nbsp;23,
2005.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(f)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>On May&nbsp;26, 2004,

signed a $2.0 million promissory note in favor of Hibernia National Bank (&#147;Hibernia&#148;).
The $2.0&nbsp;million was used by SWRG for construction costs related to the
new Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant in Boston. The note bears interest at
a fixed rate of 6.27% per annum. Principal payments for this note commenced June&nbsp;26,
2004. Pursuant to the terms of the promissory note, New Orleans is obligated to
make monthly payments of $17 for this note over the term of the note with a
balloon payment of approximately $1,548 on May&nbsp;26, 2009, the maturity date
of the note. This note is secured by a first mortgage relating to the New Orleans
property. At January&nbsp;2, 2006, New Orleans was not in compliance with the
financial covenants contained in the agreement. On March&nbsp;27, 2006, a
letter was signed by Hibernia waiving the financial covenants contained in our
promissory note for the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006 and through January&nbsp;1,
2007. SWRG is currently in the process of amending the financial covenants
contained in its promissory note with Hibernia.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;23, 2005, S&amp;W of Las Vegas, LLC (the
&#147;Borrower&#148;) entered into a Contract of Sale (the &#147;Las Vegas Agreement&#148;) with
Metroflag SW, LLC (the &#147;Buyer&#148;). Pursuant to the Las Vegas Agreement, on May&nbsp;23,
2005, (i)&nbsp;the Borrower assigned to the Buyer its existing ground lease
(the &#147;Existing Lease&#148;) in respect of the property located at 3767 Las Vegas
Boulevard South, Las Vegas, Nevada (the &#147;Las Vegas Property&#148;), (ii)&nbsp;the
Buyer purchased the Las Vegas Property pursuant to an option contained in the Existing
Lease and (iii)&nbsp;the Borrower entered into a lease-back lease (the &#147;New
Lease&#148;) pursuant to which the Borrower is leasing the Las Vegas Property. This
transaction closed on May&nbsp;23, 2005. The aggregate purchase price was
$30,000 and was paid out as follows: (a)&nbsp;approximately $10,444 to the
existing fee owner/ground lessor of the Las Vegas Property, and (b)&nbsp;the
difference between $30,000 and the amount paid to the fee owner/ground lessor
of the Las Vegas Property to the Borrower (approximately $19,556). The Borrower
received net proceeds from the transaction equal to approximately $19,300 (after
legal and other miscellaneous cost, but before taxes) and used approximately $9,200
of the net proceeds from the transactions to repay existing indebtedness. The
net gain on this &#160;transaction of
approximately $13,500 is being deferred and recognized as a reduction in rent
expense and interest expense over the life of the New Lease. At January&nbsp;3,
2005, SWRG had a deferred tax asset of $9.8 million, which was fully reserved and
included net operating loss and tax credit carryforwards of approximately $4.2
million that was reversed during the three months ended July&nbsp;4, 2005 and
was utilized against the tax gain associated with the sale of </font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p> <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

2005. In addition, a deferred tax asset of approximately $5.1 million was

At January&nbsp;2, 2006, SWRG recorded a full valuation allowance against the

benefit being realized in the future.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The New Lease has a 40 year term and requires the
Borrower to pay a negotiated fixed minimum annual rent of $1,400 for the first five
years, increasing by 5% every five years thereafter, subject to a contingent rental
provision based upon the sales of the underlying restaurant. The Las Vegas
Agreement and the New Lease contain representations, warranties, covenants and
indemnities that are typical for transactions of this kind. In accordance with
FAS 13, because the New Lease involves both land and building and the fair
value of the land is greater than 25% of the total fair value of the land and
building, the land and building are considered separate elements for applying
lease accounting criteria. The portion of the New Lease that relates to the
building is being treated as a capital lease and the portion of the New Lease
relating to the land is being treated as an operating lease.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;23, 2004, Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky
of Boston, LLC, Houston S&amp;W, L.P. and Dallas S&amp;W, L.P. (collectively,
the &#147;Lessees&#148;), each a wholly-owned subsidiary of SWRG, entered into a Master
Lease Agreement and related schedules (the &#147;Lease&#148;) with General Electric
Capital Corporation, which subsequently assigned its rights, interests and
obligations under the Lease to Ameritech Credit Corporation, d/b/a SBC Capital
Services (&#147;SBC&#148;), pursuant to which SBC acquired certain equipment and then
leased such equipment to the Lessees. The transaction enabled the Lessees to
finance approximately $1,500 of existing equipment. Subject to adjustment in
certain circumstances, the monthly rent payable under the Lease is $31. The
Lessees are treating this transaction as a sale-leaseback transaction with the
lease being classified as a capital lease and the gain recorded on the sale of
approximately $151 was deferred and is being recognized over the life of the
Lease. <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The $1,500 was used for construction
costs related to the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky restaurant in Boston. The
monthly payments were calculated using an annual interest rate of approximately
7.2%. </font>In connection with the transaction, SWRG entered into a corporate guaranty
on December&nbsp;23, 2004 to guarantee the Lessees&#146; obligations under the Lease.
<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The Lessees may after 48 months, and after
giving 30 days notice, purchase back all the equipment listed under the Lease
at a cost of approximately $405.</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 13.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The remainder of the fixed
minimum annual rental payments is being treated as an operating lease (see Note
14).</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(13)</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font>Commitments
and Contingencies</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="OperatingLeaseCommitments_104034"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating
Lease Commitments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All of SWRG&#146;s consolidated restaurants operate in
leased premises, with the exception of the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky locations
in New Orleans and Dallas, which are owned properties. Remaining lease terms
range from approximately 4 to 40&nbsp;years, including anticipated renewal
options. The leases generally provide for minimum annual rental payments and
are subject to escalations based upon increases in the Consumer Price Index,
real estate taxes and other costs. In addition, certain leases contain contingent
rental provisions based upon the sales of the underlying restaurants. Certain
leases also provide for rent deferral during the initial term of such leases
and/or scheduled minimum rent increases during the terms of the leases. Any
rent expense incurred during the construction period was capitalized as a part
of leasehold improvements and is being amortized on a straight-line basis from
the date operations commence over the remaining life of the lease, which
includes the renewal period. For any leases entered into after
September&nbsp;15, 2005, SWRG will be expensing these costs in conjunction with
the FASB Staff Position FAS 13-1, &#147;Accounting for Rental Costs Incurred
during a Construction Period&#148;. Accordingly, included in long-term liabilities
in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets at January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3,
2005 are accruals related to such rent deferrals and the pro rata portion of
scheduled rent increases of approximately $9,133 and $8,647, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;6, 2005, SWRG signed a lease agreement
for its new corporate offices with Vandergard Properties Co., L.P. The lease
term began on October&nbsp;6, 2005 and expires in February&nbsp;2016 and
contains a fixed minimum rent of $362 per annum, plus electricity, with annual
increases of $34 commencing in March&nbsp;2011. The Company took possession of
the location December&nbsp;1, 2005 to begin the buildout phase, therefore began
deferring rent and reflecting rent expense for this period. The lease agreement
for SWRG&#146;s current corporate offices expires by its terms on February&nbsp;28,
2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG is contingently liable under letters of credit
aggregating $168 at January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005,
respectively, for deposits with the landlord of one of its restaurants and the
corporate office.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rental

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="LegalMatters_105551"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Legal Matters</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On or about September&nbsp;5, 2001, Mondo&#146;s of
Scottsdale, L.C. (&#147;Mondo&#146;s&#148;) filed a suit against SWRG alleging that it had
entered into an agreement to purchase all of the leasehold interest in, and
certain fixtures and equipment located at, Mondo&#146;s restaurant located in
Scottsdale, Arizona. The suit was filed in the Superior Court of the State of
Arizona in and for the County of Maricopa and had been set to go to jury trial
in March&nbsp;2004. The plaintiff requested damages of approximately $2.0
million. On March&nbsp;18, 2004, the parties tentatively agreed to settle the
matter for $525 and a reserve of $525 was established as of December&nbsp;29,
2003. On April&nbsp;9, 2004 a final settlement was reached between the parties
and, in accordance with the settlement, SWRG made the first payment of $225 on April&nbsp;9,
2004 and the final payment of $300 on April&nbsp;11, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;22, 2004, Parade 59, LLC (&#147;Parade&#148;),
a wholly owned subsidiary of SWRG that managed the ONEc.p.s. restaurant in the
Plaza Hotel, filed suit against Plaza Operating Partners ELAD </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">31</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-31',FILE='C:\fc\9018464409_F25892_987929\7678-1-fu.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar 31 18:46 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Properties, LLC and CPS1,
LLC (collectively the &#147;Defendants&#148;) alleging that the Defendants (1)&nbsp;failed
to pay a base management fee to Parade as provided for in the restaurant management
agreement described above, (2)&nbsp;failed to pay hotel, guest, room and credit
account charges to Parade, and (3)&nbsp;failed to pay termination costs to
Parade in connection with the termination of the restaurant management
agreement. On February&nbsp;28, 2005, the Defendants served their answers and
counterclaims against Parade alleging, among other things, that Parade (1)&nbsp;failed
to make payments, (2)&nbsp;breached a memorandum of understanding and other
agreements and (3)&nbsp;is liable for attorney fees and costs, with damages
totaling no less than $3.5 million. SWRG believes that it will likely prevail
in these matters and that the risk of material loss is not probable.
Accordingly, SWRG has not established a reserve for loss in connection with the
counterclaims. If Parade were to lose the counterclaims, its financial
position, results of operations and cash flows could be adversely affected. As
of January&nbsp;2, 2006 there were no changes to the status of these claims or
counterclaims.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG is involved in
various claims and legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business. In
the opinion of management, the ultimate disposition of these matters will not
have a material adverse effect on SWRG&#146;s consolidated financial position,
results of operations or liquidity.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="EmploymentAndNoncompetitionAgreem_105554"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employment

Company&#146;s Chief Executive Officer to a minimum salary, as well as an annual
bonus based on targets set by its Board of Directors. On January&nbsp;31, 2006,
SWRG announced that it intends to enter into a new five year employment
agreement with the Company&#146;s current Chief Executive Officer.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;4, 2005, the Board of Directors (&#147;Board&#148;)
of SWRG adopted a Management Retention Plan (&#147;2005 Plan&#148;). The Board adopted
the plan in recognition of the importance to SWRG and its stockholders of
assuring that SWRG has the continued dedication and full attention of certain
key employees notwithstanding the possibility, threat or occurrence of a change
in control, as defined in the </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;30, 2005, SWRG signed a Separation
Agreement with James M. Dunn, its former President and General Manager of the
Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky in Boston. In exchange for Mr.&nbsp;Dunn&#146;s execution
of the Separation Agreement, SWRG is obligated to pay Mr.&nbsp;Dunn $10 per
month from August&nbsp;1, 2005 until April&nbsp;30, 2006. SWRG expensed the
entire obligation to Mr.&nbsp;Dunn in fiscal 2005. In addition, SWRG agreed to
purchase any shares of common stock that Mr.&nbsp;Dunn was to receive upon the
exercise of his stock options at a price of $6.00 per share, less the exercise
price of $3.88 per share. On August&nbsp;30, 2005, SWRG purchased 158,667
shares of common stock from Mr.&nbsp;Dunn. &#160;This purchase resulted in a compensation
expense to SWRG of $336.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Includes the accounts

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Includes the accounts
and results of the entity that owns M&amp;P as a direct result of adoption of
FIN46(R). See Note 2</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In assessing the realizability of deferred tax assets,
management considers whether it is more likely than not that some portion or
all of the deferred tax assets will be realized. The ultimate realization of
deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income
during the periods in which </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">34</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">temporary differences
become deductible and net operating losses and tax credits can be carried
forward. Management considers projected future taxable income and tax planning
strategies in making this assessment. After consideration of SWRG&#146;s operating
losses in recent years and projections for future taxable income over the
period, against which the deferred tax assets are deductible, a full valuation
allowance has been established against SWRG&#146;s net deferred tax assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At January&nbsp;3, 2005,
SWRG had a deferred tax asset of $9,848, which was fully reserved and included
net operating loss and tax credit&#160;
carryforwards&#160; of approximately
$4,200 that was reversed during the three months ended July&nbsp;4, 2005 and
was utilized&#160; against the tax gain&#160; associated&#160;
with the sale of the Las Vegas&#160;
property&#160; on May&nbsp;23,&#160; 2005. In addition, a deferred tax asset of
approximately $5,100 was recorded during the three months ended July&nbsp;4,
2005 for the temporary difference on the deferred gain relating to the sale of
the Las Vegas property. As of January&nbsp;2, 2006, SWRG has a full valuation
allowance against the net deferred tax asset of $10,995, due to the uncertainty
of this benefit being realized in the future. These tax credit carryforwards
exist in federal and certain state jurisdictions and have varying carryforward
periods and restrictions on usage. The estimation of future taxable income for
federal and state purposes and SWRG&#146;s resulting ability to utilize tax credit
carryforwards can significantly change based on future events and operating
results. Thus, recorded valuation allowances may be subject to material future
changes.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(15)</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160; </font>Common
Stock</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2001 Stock Incentive Plan (&#147;2001 Stock Incentive
Plan&#148;) provides for the granting of options to purchase shares of our common
stock and stock awards. Options may be incentive stock options, as defined in Section&nbsp;422
of the Internal Revenue Code (the &#147;Code&#148;), granted only to our employees
(including officers who are also employees) or non-qualified stock options
granted to our employees, directors, officers and consultants. Stock awards may
be granted to employees of, and other key individuals engaged to provide
services to, SWRG and its subsidiaries. The 2001 Stock Incentive Plan was
adopted and approved by our directors in March&nbsp;2001 and our stockholders
in April&nbsp;2001<b><font style="font-weight:bold;">.</font></b></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2001 Stock Incentive Plan may be administered by
our Board of Directors or by our Compensation Committee, either of which may
decide who will receive stock option or stock awards, the amount of the awards,
and the terms and conditions associated with the awards. These include the
price at which stock options may be exercised, the conditions for vesting or
accelerated vesting, acceptable methods for paying for shares, the effect of
corporate transactions or changes in control, and the events triggering
expiration or forfeiture of a participant&#146;s rights. The maximum term for stock
options may not exceed ten years, provided that no incentive stock options may
be granted to any employee who owns ten percent or more of SWRG with a term
exceeding five years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The maximum number of shares of common stock available
for issuance under the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan is 583,333 shares, increased
by 4% of the total number of issued and outstanding shares of common stock
(including shares held in treasury) as of the close of business on December&nbsp;31
of the preceding year on each January&nbsp;1, beginning with January&nbsp;1,
2002, during the term of the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan. However, the number of
shares available for all grants under the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan is limited
to 11% of SWRG&#146;s issued and outstanding shares of capital stock on a fully-diluted
basis. Accordingly, the maximum number of options to purchase shares of common
stock available for issuance in 2005 was approximately 213,000 shares. In
addition, options may not be granted to any individual with </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">35</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">respect to more than
500,000 total shares of common stock in any single taxable year (taking into
account options that were terminated, repriced, or otherwise adjusted during
such taxable year).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2001 Stock Incentive Plan provides that
proportionate adjustments will be made to the number of authorized shares which
may be granted under the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan and as to which outstanding
options, or portions of outstanding options, then unexercised will be
exercisable as a result of increases or decreases in SWRG&#146;s outstanding shares
of common stock due to reorganization, merger, consolidation, recapitalization,
reclassification, stock split-up, combination of shares, or dividends payable
in capital stock, such that the proportionate interest of the option holder
will be maintained as before the occurrence of such event. Upon the sale or
conveyance to another entity of all or substantially all of the property and
assets of SWRG, including by way of a merger or consolidation or a Change in
Control of SWRG, as defined in the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan, our Board of
Directors will have the power and the right to accelerate the exercisability of
any options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unless sooner terminated by our Board of Directors,
the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan will terminate on April&nbsp;30, 2011, ten years
from the date on which the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan was adopted by our Board
of Directors. All options granted under the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan will
terminate immediately prior to the dissolution or liquidation of SWRG;
provided, that prior to such dissolution or liquidation, the vesting of any
option will automatically accelerate as if such dissolution or liquidation is
deemed a Change of Control, as defined in the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September&nbsp;5, 2002, SWRG granted options
pursuant to an option exchange program (the &#147;Option Exchange Program&#148;) that
SWRG initiated in February&nbsp;2002 in order to allow employees, officers and
directors to cancel all or some stock options to purchase its common stock
having an exercise price greater than $5.70 per share granted under its 1996
Stock Option Plan, its 1997 Stock Option Plan and its 2001 Stock Incentive Plan
in exchange for new options granted under the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan. Under
the Option Exchange Program, the new options were issued on September&nbsp;5,
2002 with an exercise price of $3.88. The exercise price of each option
received under the exchange program equaled 100% of the price of SWRG&#146;s common
stock on the date of grant of the new options, determined in accordance with
the terms of the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan. An employee received options under
the exchange program with an exercise price of $4.27, or 110% of the fair
market value of SWRG&#146;s common stock on the date of grant. The new options vest
over periods ranging from four months to five years, in accordance with the
vesting schedule of the cancelled options. SWRG structured the Option Exchange
Program in a manner that did not result in any additional compensation charges
or variable award accounting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;and July&nbsp;2003, SWRG granted options
to purchase 127,000 shares of common stock under the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan.
The weighted average exercise price of the options granted was $5.05 per share,
the estimated fair market value of the underlying common shares at the date of
grant. Each option granted in June&nbsp;and July&nbsp;2003 will vest over a
period of five years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2004, SWRG granted options to purchase
83,500 shares of common stock under the 2001 Stock Incentive Plan. The weighted
average exercise price of the options granted was $5.70 per share, the fair
market value of the underlying common shares at the date of grant. Each option
granted in August&nbsp;2004 will vest over a period of five years. An employee
received options under this grant with an exercise price of $6.27, or 110% of
the fair market value of SWRG&#146;s common stock on the date of grant.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><a name="a16TreasuryStock_095653"></a><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a16TreasuryStock_101909"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(16) Treasury Stock</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;24,&#160;
2005,&#160; SWRG&#160; announced&#160;
that the Board of Directors of SWRG had authorized a stock&#160; repurchase&#160;
program under which up to one million&#160;
shares of its common stock were authorized to be </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">37</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-37',FILE='C:\fc\93134112464_F25892_993439\7678-1-fw.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Apr  3 13:41 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">THE SMITH&nbsp;&amp; WOLLENSKY RESTAURANT GROUP, INC.<br> AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></b></p> <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements January&nbsp;2, 2006 and January&nbsp;3, 2005 (Continued)<br> (in thousands, except shares and per share/unit amounts)</font></b></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">acquired in the open
market over the 18 months following such authorization at the discretion of
management.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The shares are purchased from time to time at
prevailing market price through open market or unsolicited negotiated
transactions, depending on market conditions. Under&#160; the&#160;
program, the purchases are funded from available working capital, and
the repurchased shares are held in treasury or used for ongoing stock issuances.
There is no guarantee as to the exact number of shares which will be
repurchased by SWRG, and SWRG may discontinue purchases at any time that
management determines additional purchases are not warranted.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Treasury stock is recorded at net acquisition cost.
Gains and losses on disposition are recorded as increases or decreases to
additional paid-in capital with losses in excess of previously recorded gains
charged directly to retained earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
the fiscal year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006, SWRG reacquired 927,114 shares of
common stock pursuant to an approved, open market repurchase plan. Of the
927,114 shares of common stock acquired, pursuant to the&#160; approved plan, 158,667 shares were acquired
from James M. Dunn, the former President and General Manager of the Smith&nbsp;&amp;
Wollensky in Boston and 41,000 shares were acquired from Alan M. Mandel, the
former Chief Financial Officer. SWRG recorded a compensation expense of $408 in
conjunction with these purchases. The shares acquired through open market
purchases have not been formally retired and, accordingly, are carried as
treasury stock.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a17HurricaneImpact_101927"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(17) Impairment of Assets Impacted by Hurricane</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;29, 2005, Hurricane Katrina hit the
Gulf Coast, causing damage to the Smith&nbsp;&amp; Wollensky unit in New
Orleans, Louisiana (&#147;S&amp;W of New Orleans&#148;). As of January&nbsp;2, 2006, SWRG
is working closely with its insurance carriers and claims adjusters to
ascertain the full amount of damages. SWRG is in the process of having an adjuster
determine the total extent of the damages. As of January&nbsp;2, 2006, SWRG is
unable to determine the extent of the necessary repairs or when this restaurant
will reopen.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SWRG
maintains insurance policies that cover certain losses relating to flood and
wind damage for S&amp;W of New Orleans. SWRG is not currently able to estimate
whether potential insurance proceeds, net of deductible and related expenses,
are expected to equal or exceed the net book value of the impacted assets. SWRG
has recorded an impairment of $750 which includes an estimate of the maximum
deductible which could be incurred under our insurance policy as well as an
estimate of other impaired assets not believed to be covered under our insurance
policy. This amount is net of $100 of insurance proceeds received related to
content coverage. SWRG has also written off approximately $160 in inventories
that spoiled or were destroyed by Hurricane Katrina. SWRG&#146;s insurance policies
also provide coverage for interruption to the S&amp;W of New Orleans&#146; business,
including lost profits, and reimbursement of certain expenses. SWRG received advances
of $350 for business interruption which is reflected in its statement of
operations for the year ended January&nbsp;2, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a18GiftCardLiability_101933"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(18) Gift Card Liability</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2005,
a new gift card tracking system was implemented to track the gift card
liability. For gift cards issued prior to April&nbsp;2005, SWRG used its best
estimate to establish a liability for gift certificates issued , but not
redeemed prior to April&nbsp;2005 (&#147;Old Gift Certificates&#148;). Based on the
redemption of Old </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">38</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">
